Diagnostic testing confirmed acute COVID-19 by RT-PCR and Mycobacterium tuberculosis by GeneXpert. Laboratory monitoring of HIV demonstrated an elevated HIV-1 RNA viral load of 9,000 copies/mL and a CD4 count of 266 cells/mm3. HAART was continued throughout inpatient management. Quantitative HIV-1 RNA viral load provides conclusive E1 confirmatory laboratory evidence. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Ms PM, a 28-year-old female with HIV infection presenting with severe respiratory distress, wasting, oral candidiasis, and multiple thin-walled lung cysts

step5_concept_grounding: Documented human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection complicated by severe wasting, oral candidiasis, normocytic anemia, and bilateral thin-walled pulmonary cysts

evidence_items.source_quote: Ms PM is a 28-year-old female, originally from Eastern Cape Province in South Africa (SA).
Blood results showed acute kidney injury (resolved with crystalloid fluids), a raised c-reactive protein (CRP) of 143 mmol/L, and a normocytic anaemia attributed to her HIV infection.
evidence_items.test_name: Clinical diagnostic attribution and blood analysis

rationale: A 28-year-old female (Ms PM) presented with severe respiratory distress, profound wasting, oral candidiasis, and septic shock, with chest radiography demonstrating diffuse bilateral thin-walled pulmonary cysts. Laboratory evaluation demonstrated acute kidney injury, marked systemic inflammation, and normocytic anemia explicitly attributed by attending clinicians to her underlying HIV infection. The clinical constellation of advanced wasting, opportunistic oral candidiasis, and confirmed diagnosis of HIV infection establishes confirmed disease status -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A patient (38-year-old female from Central Africa) with HIV infection who developed Kaposi disease (KD) following vascular trauma

step5_concept_grounding: Documented HIV infection in an adult patient from Central Africa presenting with Kaposi disease occurring after vascular trauma

evidence_items.source_quote: We report here a case of KD occurring after a 10-year-old vascular trauma on a patient from Central Africa with HIV infection.

rationale: This clinical case report introduces and reports a patient from Central Africa with documented HIV infection who developed Kaposi disease (an AIDS-defining illness) 10 years after localized vascular trauma. The narrative explicitly asserts HIV infection in an individual human patient presenting with classic HIV-associated Kaposi disease. The presence of confirmed HIV infection meets positive diagnostic criteria -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 38-year-old woman from Central Africa presenting with painful purple papules and macules on her right leg diagnosed with HIV-1 infection and epidemic Kaposi disease

step5_concept_grounding: Newly diagnosed HIV-1 infection confirmed by positive serology with CD4 count of 600 cells/mm3, presenting with epidemic Kaposi disease treated successfully with emtricitabine-tenofovir and efavirenz

evidence_items.source_quote: HIV serology was positive to HIV1. The CD4 count was 600 cells/mm3. The diagnosis of epidemic KD on an anteriorly traumatized leg in a patient from Central Africa was retained.
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV-1 antibody serology and CD4 T-cell count

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient was put on a combination of antiretrovirals including two nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (emtricitabine-tenofovir) and a non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (efavirenz).

rationale: A 38-year-old woman from Central Africa presented with a 6-month history of painful violaceous macules and angiomatous papulo-nodules on her right lower extremity at the site of prior trauma. Diagnostic workup confirmed HIV-1 infection with positive retroviral serology and a CD4 count of 600 cells/mm3, establishing a diagnosis of epidemic Kaposi disease. Combination antiretroviral therapy with emtricitabine, tenofovir, and efavirenz resulted in resolution of pain and substantial regression of lesions after 6 months. Conclusive positive serology and initiation of combination ART establish confirmed diagnosis -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 29-year-old male mountain climber presenting with high-altitude retinopathy and vitreous hemorrhage, screened negative for HIV

step5_concept_grounding: Exclusion of HIV infection during routine systemic and infectious workup of high-altitude retinopathy and retinal venous dilation

evidence_items.source_quote: Full blood count, haemoglobin, sugar, creatinine, urea, lipids, CRP, and serology for HIV, HCV, VDRL, and HBsAg were normal.

rationale: A 29-year-old male presenting with left eye floaters and decreased visual acuity following high-altitude mountaineering (4,760 m) was diagnosed with bilateral high-altitude retinopathy and vitreous hemorrhage. Laboratory screening including HIV serology was normal and negative. Because HIV was specifically tested and ruled out, the label is NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 12-year-old girl with vertically acquired HIV on ART experiencing complex treatment failure, extensive drug resistance mutations, and psychosocial adherence barriers

step5_concept_grounding: Perinatally acquired HIV-1 infection with multi-class drug resistance (NRTI, NNRTI, PI, and INSTI mutations on genotypic testing) requiring third-line and holding antiretroviral regimens

evidence_items.source_quote: At the time of the referral, the patient was 12 years old and living in Pretoria with her aunt. Her mother lived in Limpopo and was also using ART. The patient was aware of her HIV status and it was known to all her close adult family members. She reported poor adherence with her ART treatment because it was unpalatable.

She had three genotypic drug resistance tests (DRTs) over the next 2 years and the mutations evolved from low-level resistance to ritonavir-boosted lopinavir to extensive three-class resistance during this time (Table 1).
She is now on a holding regimen consisting of FTC, TDF, AZT and abacavir (ABC). A tropism assay predicted that CCR5-antagonists are likely to be effective.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV coreceptor tropism assay and holding regimen

rationale: A 12-year-old girl with known vertically transmitted HIV infection on long-term antiretroviral therapy presented with virologic failure secondary to poor treatment adherence. Over longitudinal follow-up, four sequential HIV genotypic drug resistance tests (DRTs) demonstrated extensive multi-class antiretroviral resistance mutations spanning NRTIs, NNRTIs, PIs, and integrase strand transfer inhibitors (INSTIs). Viral load rebound and viral tropism assays confirmed active viral replication. Documented HIV molecular resistance sequencing establishes conclusive E1 confirmatory evidence -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 27-year-old Thai male with AIDS on ART presenting with acute abdominal pain, splenic abscess, and disseminated Talaromyces marneffei infection

step5_concept_grounding: Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) and HIV infection with severe CD4 lymphopenia (nadir 91 cells/mm3, admission 272 cells/mm3) on ART complicated by disseminated Talaromyces marneffei

evidence_items.source_quote: A 27-year-old Thai male with AIDS from Saraburi Province presented with acute abdominal pain that had lasted for 4 days.

He was diagnosed with AIDS 2 months before at another hospital, which recorded an initial CD4 count of 91 cells/mm3 (unknown percentage and HIV viral load) and no complete immune status evaluation was performed.
evidence_items.test_name: Initial CD4 count at AIDS diagnosis

evidence_items.source_quote: The CD4 count on admission was 272 cells/mm3 (19%).

rationale: A 27-year-old male with an established diagnosis of AIDS, prior Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, and baseline CD4 lymphopenia of 91 cells/mm3 who had initiated combination antiretroviral therapy (tenofovir, emtricitabine, efavirenz) presented with acute left upper quadrant abdominal pain and high fever. Blood and bone marrow cultures confirmed disseminated Talaromyces marneffei. Admission CD4 count showed immune reconstitution to 272 cells/mm3 (19%). Confirmed AIDS diagnosis with CD4 monitoring and characteristic opportunistic infections meets confirmatory criteria -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A community case study documenting public health cervical cancer prevention and screening programs in Uganda; no individual patient clinical case

step5_concept_grounding: Population-level public health policy on cervical cancer screening guidelines for HIV-positive versus HIV-negative women in Uganda
rationale: This article is a Community Case Study describing a complex health systems intervention for cervical cancer screening in Uganda. Mention of HIV is limited to background national policy guidelines regarding recommended screening frequencies (annual for HIV-positive women vs every 3 years for HIV-negative women). The paper reports program implementation and community health strategies rather than an individual clinical case unit (F2_SCOPE_COHORT). Excluded as non-single patient aggregate study -> EXCLUDED_NON_SINGLE_PATIENT.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 38-year-old male presenting with weight loss and anorexia, newly diagnosed with HIV infection, severe CD4 depletion (2 cells/muL), and cryptococcal antigenemia

step5_concept_grounding: Newly diagnosed advanced HIV-1 infection with profound CD4 lymphopenia (2 cells/muL) and asymptomatic cryptococcal antigenemia treated with fluconazole and ART

evidence_items.source_quote: A 38-year-old male was seen at his local clinic with a 6-month history of loss of weight (approximately 10 kg) and progressive loss of appetite. A rapid HIV test was performed and was positive. Additional blood tests confirmed a CD4 cell count of 2 cells/muL and a positive CrAg LFA.
evidence_items.test_name: Rapid HIV test and CD4 cell count
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV antibodies and CD4 lymphocyte count

evidence_items.source_quote: At the 2-week follow-up visit, the fluconazole dose was reduced to 400 mg daily and ART:with tenofovir, emtricitibine, and efavirenz:was initiated.

rationale: A 38-year-old male presented with a 6-month history of weight loss and anorexia. Diagnostic testing at a local clinic confirmed a positive rapid HIV test, a CD4 cell count of 2 cells/muL indicating severe immunosuppression, and a positive cryptococcal lateral flow assay. Lumbar puncture excluded cryptococcal meningitis. Preemptive antifungal therapy with fluconazole was initiated, followed by combination antiretroviral therapy (tenofovir, emtricitabine, efavirenz). Positive rapid HIV testing in conjunction with profound CD4 lymphopenia and initiation of ART establishes confirmed HIV diagnosis -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 37-year-old female diagnosed with HIV two years previously on ART presenting with cryptococcal meningitis and unmasking HIV-associated immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome

step5_concept_grounding: Established HIV-1 infection with severe CD4 lymphopenia (76 cells/muL) on ART presenting with unmasking cryptococcal meningitis IRIS

evidence_items.source_quote: She had no medical history of TB but was diagnosed with HIV two years ago. At a visit to her local clinic about 3 weeks before this admission, laboratory tests showed a CD4 cell count of 76 cells/muL. She was subsequently started on antiretroviral therapy:with tenofovir, emtricitabine, and efavirenz.
evidence_items.test_name: Documented HIV history, CD4 count, and ART

evidence_items.source_quote: A diagnosis was made of cryptococcal meningitis with raised intracranial pressure and unmasking HIV-associated IRIS. ART was continued in the ward, and antifungal therapy was started with amphotericin B (1 mg/kg/day IV) and high dose fluconazole of 800 mg daily.

rationale: A 37-year-old female with HIV diagnosed two years prior was started on combination ART (tenofovir, emtricitabine, efavirenz) following demonstration of severe CD4 depletion (76 cells/muL). Three weeks later, she presented with acute headache, fever, and neck stiffness, diagnosed with cryptococcal meningitis and unmasking HIV-associated immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS). Antifungal therapy was administered and ART was continued. Established HIV infection with low CD4 count on ART complicated by IRIS confirms active disease -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 28-year-old male with known HIV infection since 2010 presenting with chronic monoarthritis and disseminated paracoccidioidomycosis

step5_concept_grounding: Established HIV infection with severe CD4 lymphopenia (44 cells/mm3) on first-line ART presenting with fatal disseminated Paracoccidioides brasiliensis

evidence_items.source_quote: A 28-year-old male from Santarem, Para, Brazil, with a history of leisure activities in a rural area, tractor driver, a known carrier of the HIV virus since 2010, however without previous follow-up, contacted us for the first time at Fundacao de Medicina Tropical Dr. Heitor Vieira Dourado, Manaus, Amazonas, Brazil, for investigation of left knee chronic monoarthritis associated with tegumentary lesions. He had been using zidovudine, lamivudine, lopinavir/ritonavir for three weeks, this being the first antiretroviral regimen used.
evidence_items.test_name: Documented HIV infection history and ART

evidence_items.source_quote: At the time of diagnosis T CD4+ count was 44 cells/mm3 .

rationale: A 28-year-old male known carrier of HIV since 2010 who had initiated antiretroviral therapy (zidovudine, lamivudine, lopinavir/ritonavir) 3 weeks earlier presented with chronic left knee monoarthritis and extensive polymorphic cutaneous lesions. Synovial and skin biopsy confirmed Paracoccidioides brasiliensis infection. Laboratory evaluation revealed profound immunosuppression with a CD4 count of 44 cells/mm3. Despite amphotericin B therapy, he succumbed to disseminated multi-organ paracoccidioidomycosis. Established HIV infection with profound CD4 lymphopenia and active ART confirms disease presence -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 39-year-old female with well-controlled HIV on HAART and ESRD secondary to HIV-associated nephropathy, presenting with malignant ascites from omental extramedullary plasmacytoma

step5_concept_grounding: Documented HIV infection of 6 years on HAART with ESRD secondary to biopsy-proven HIV-associated nephropathy (HIVAN), CD4 count 600/mm3, and viral load 986 copies/mL

evidence_items.source_quote: Her past medical history was significant for a well-controlled HIV infection of 6 years on highly active anti-retroviral therapy, hypertension, ESRD secondary to HIV-associated nephropathy, and secondary hyperparathyroidism.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV medical history and biopsy-proven HIVAN
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV infection on HAART and HIV-associated nephropathy

evidence_items.source_quote: CD4 T-cell count: 600/mm3, HIV viral load: 986 copies/mL (reference: < 40 copies/mL), serum creatinine: 10.3 mg/dL
evidence_items.test_name: HIV quantitative RNA viral load and CD4 count
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV-1 viral load and CD4 count

rationale: A 39-year-old female with a 6-year history of HIV on HAART and end-stage renal disease secondary to biopsy-proven collapsing focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (HIV-associated nephropathy) presented with recurrent large-volume ascites diagnosed as omental extramedullary plasmacytoma. Laboratory evaluation confirmed active HIV monitoring with a CD4 count of 600 cells/mm3 and a detectable HIV RNA viral load of 986 copies/mL. Quantitative viral load provides E1 confirmatory evidence of HIV infection -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 60-year-old European homosexual male diagnosed with HIV in 1985 on long-term ART with immunological non-recovery (CD4 <140) and chronic relapsing visceral leishmaniasis

step5_concept_grounding: Longstanding HIV-1 infection diagnosed in 1985 on suppressive ART with persistent CD4 lymphopenia (nadir 39 cells/muL, ceiling 140 cells/muL) complicated by chronic refractory Leishmania infantum visceral leishmaniasis

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient was a 60 year old European homosexual man who had HIV infection diagnosed in 1985. Zidovudine monotherapy was commenced in 1988 and three-drug combination antiretroviral therapy (ART) in 1996. His ART between 2001 and 2013 consisted of lopinavir/ritonavir, lamivudine and nevirapine. He had a prompt sustained response to ART and from 1997-2013 consistently had an undetectable HIV viral load. Despite this, his CD4 count, which had a nadir of 39 in 1996, never rose above 140 despite consistent adherence to his ART (Fig 1A).
evidence_items.test_name: Longitudinal HIV viral load and CD4 monitoring on ART
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV-1 viral load and CD4 lymphocyte counts

rationale: A 60-year-old male diagnosed with HIV infection in 1985 received antiretroviral therapy spanning over two decades (zidovudine from 1988, combination ART from 1996) achieving sustained undetectable HIV viral loads from 1997 to 2013, despite blunted CD4 reconstitution (nadir 39, maximum <140 cells/muL). He developed chronic relapsing Leishmania infantum visceral leishmaniasis refractory to multiple antileishmanial regimens. Longstanding confirmed HIV infection with longitudinal viral load suppression on ART fulfills confirmatory diagnostic criteria -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 37-year-old Japanese male presenting with mandibular bone necrosis and necrotizing stomatitis, newly diagnosed with HIV-1 infection and AIDS

step5_concept_grounding: Newly diagnosed HIV-1 infection (anti-HIV antibody positive, CD4 count 78/muL, plasma HIV-RNA load 250,000 copies/mL) presenting with extensive mandibular osteonecrosis and necrotizing stomatitis

evidence_items.source_quote: HIV enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay testing showed positive results. The patient was found to be anti-HIV-antibody positive. The patient then reported he was homosexual. His CD4 count was 78/muL, and the plasma HIV-RNA load was 2.5 x 105 copies/mL.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV ELISA, anti-HIV antibody, CD4 count, and HIV-RNA viral load
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV antibody, CD4 count, and HIV-RNA

evidence_items.source_quote: HAART was started with emtricitabine at 200 mg/day, tenofovir disoproxil fumarate/abacavir at 300 mg/day, and raltegravir potassium at 1600 mg/day to treat AIDS, followed by ethambutol at 1000 mg/day, rifampicin at 300 mg/day, clarythromycin at 800 mg/day, and ciprofloxacin at 1200 mg/day for the non-tuberculous mycobacterial infection.
One month after initiating HAART, the HIV-RNA load markedly decreased (from 2.5 x 105 copies/mL to less than 44 copies/mL), but the CD4 count was 78/muL.

rationale: A 37-year-old male presented with severe mandibular pain, tooth loosening, and osteonecrosis with exposed cortical bone and necrotizing ulcerative stomatitis. Infectious workup revealed positive HIV ELISA testing, positive anti-HIV antibodies, profound CD4 depletion (78/muL), and a plasma HIV-RNA load of 2.5 x 10^5 copies/mL. He was started on HAART (emtricitabine, tenofovir/abacavir, raltegravir), achieving rapid virological suppression to <44 copies/mL and subsequent CD4 recovery to 280/muL with spontaneous healing and bony remodeling. Definitive ELISA serology and quantitative viral load PCR establish E1 confirmatory diagnosis -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 54-year-old male with HIV infection on HAART presenting with retinal necrosis, hemorrhages, and severe vitritis secondary to CMV retinitis / immune recovery uveitis

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection on HAART (AZT+3TC+EFV) with CD4 lymphopenia (200/muL) presenting with cytomegalovirus retinitis and immune recovery vitritis

evidence_items.source_quote: A 54-year-old male experienced blurred vision in the right eye 2 months after HAART initiation (Zidovudine [AZT], Lamivudine [3TC], and Efavirenz [EFV]). CD4 counts were 200/mul.
evidence_items.test_name: HAART initiation and CD4 cell count
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV infection on HAART and CD4 count

rationale: A 54-year-old male with HIV infection initiated on highly active antiretroviral therapy (zidovudine, lamivudine, efavirenz) presented two months post-initiation with acute visual deterioration (VA 20/166), retinal necrosis, and severe vitritis. Laboratory evaluation showed a CD4 count of 200/muL and vitreous CMV DNA sequencing of 66,544 copies, confirming cytomegalovirus retinitis and immune recovery uveitis. Confirmed HIV infection established on multi-agent HAART with documented CD4 depletion satisfies criteria -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 40-year-old male with HIV infection on HAART presenting with bilateral blurred vision, retinal necrosis, and secondary retinal detachment from CMV retinitis / immune recovery uveitis

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection on HAART (3TC and dolutegravir) with CD4 lymphopenia (160/muL) presenting with bilateral CMV retinitis and vitritis

evidence_items.source_quote: A 40-year-old male experienced blurred vision and black shadows in both eyes 2 months after HAART initiation (3TC and Dolutegravir [DTG]). CD4 counts were 160/mul.
evidence_items.test_name: HAART initiation and CD4 cell count
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV infection on HAART and CD4 count

rationale: A 40-year-old male with HIV infection initiated on HAART (lamivudine and dolutegravir) developed bilateral blurred vision and vitreous floaters two months later. Clinical evaluation showed retinal necrosis, hemorrhages, and moderate vitritis with a CD4 count of 160/muL and vitreous CMV DNA sequencing of 446,072 copies, confirming CMV retinitis and immune recovery uveitis. Pars plana vitrectomy and intravitreal ganciclovir injections preserved visual acuity. Documented HIV infection established on combination HAART with marked CD4 depletion satisfies criteria -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 6-year-old male with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) presenting with fever and axillary lymphadenopathy diagnosed as benign plexiform neurofibroma, screened negative for HIV

step5_concept_grounding: Exclusion of HIV infection during serological workup for fever of unknown origin and extensive mediastinal/axillary mass lesions in a child with NF1

evidence_items.source_quote: In serological tests, VZV-IgG, EBV-VCA-IgG, and CMV-IgG were avidite positive; Hepatitis B Ag, Anti-HIV, Anti-HAV IgG and IgM, Anti-HCV, EBV-VCA IgM and VZV-IgM were negative.

rationale: A 6-year-old boy with neurofibromatosis type 1 presented with persistent high fever, leukocytosis, elevated acute phase reactants, and massive mediastino-cervico-axillary lymphadenopathy. Diagnostic infectious serology explicitly tested for anti-HIV antibodies and was negative. Histological examination of a surgical biopsy confirmed benign neurofibroma. Because HIV infection was directly evaluated and ruled out by laboratory serology, the label is NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 36-year-old Caucasian male with a 15-year history of HIV presenting with severe skin lesions diagnosed with malignant syphilis and progression to AIDS

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection progressing to acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) with CD4 count of 57 cells/muL and HIV RNA 365,000 copies/mL, complicated by malignant secondary syphilis and osteitis

evidence_items.source_quote: A 36-year-old Caucasian, homosexual male with known human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection for the past 15 years presented with a disseminated skin eruption over 6 weeks.
The CD4 count was 57 cells/muL and HIV RNA was 365,000 copies/mL.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV RNA viral load and CD4 count

rationale: A 36-year-old male with a 15-year history of untreated HIV presented with widespread ostraceous skin lesions and joint pain. Evaluation demonstrated malignant secondary syphilis osteitis, and laboratory workup confirmed late-stage HIV/AIDS with an HIV RNA viral load of 365,000 copies/mL and a nadir CD4 count of 57 cells/muL. He was treated for syphilis with doxycycline and initiated on combination antiretroviral therapy (darunavir/cobicistat, dolutegravir, tenofovir/emtricitabine) and PCP prophylaxis. Active HIV infection with confirmatory high viral load and profound CD4 depletion meets diagnostic criteria -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 64-year-old male presenting with nuchal and facial swelling and impetiginized herpes zoster, found to have myelodysplastic syndrome (RAEB II)

step5_concept_grounding: Evaluation and exclusion of HIV infection in an immunocompromised patient with impetiginized herpes zoster and myelodysplastic syndrome

evidence_items.source_quote: HIV tests were negative.

rationale: A 64-year-old male presented with fever, chills, and severe left facial and nuchal swelling diagnosed as impetiginized herpes zoster and later zoster generalisatus. Given his severe immunosuppression and clinical course, HIV testing was performed as part of the infectious/immunological evaluation and was explicitly negative. Bone marrow biopsy subsequently confirmed myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS RAEB II) as the underlying cause of immunosuppression. With HIV definitively ruled out by negative laboratory testing, this case is negative -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 31-year-old HIV-infected woman on 4-year antiretroviral therapy presenting with SJS/TEN spectrum reaction after doubling her missed ARV dose

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection established on long-term antiretroviral therapy (nevirapine, tenofovir, lamivudine), presenting with Stevens-Johnson syndrome / toxic epidermal necrolysis overlap after doubling missed doses

evidence_items.source_quote: A 31-year-old HIV-infected black African female presented with an 8-day history of painful swallowing, sore eyes, malaise and a worsening rash.
The last HIV RNA viral load test, done 11 months prior to the onset of her symptoms showed an undetectable viral load.

rationale: A 31-year-old female with confirmed HIV infection on antiretroviral therapy (nevirapine, tenofovir, and lamivudine) for over four years presented with 10% body surface area epidermal necrolysis and conjunctivitis following an accidental double dose of her ARVs. Her medical records confirmed a nadir CD4 count of 139 cells/mm3 prior to ART initiation and an undetectable HIV RNA viral load 11 months prior. Her ARVs were temporarily stopped until re-epithelialization, followed by safe transition to a fixed-dose combination regimen (Odimune). Documented established HIV infection with virological monitoring and ongoing ART satisfies confirmation -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 27-year-old Hispanic man presenting with cryptococcal and varicella zoster virus dual meningitis, evaluated for underlying immunodeficiency

step5_concept_grounding: Evaluation and exclusion of acute HIV infection in a young adult presenting with cryptococcal and VZV meningitis

evidence_items.source_quote: HIV testing was negative, and the CD4 count was within the normal range (Table 2).

rationale: A 27-year-old man presented with headaches, myalgias, and fever, found to have dual fungal and viral meningitis caused by Cryptococcus neoformans and Varicella zoster virus. Because cryptococcal meningitis in a young patient strongly raises clinical suspicion for underlying HIV infection, an acute HIV evaluation and CD4 count were performed. HIV testing was negative and CD4 counts were normal. Further immunologic workup revealed an isolated NK cell deficiency and hypocomplementemia. HIV infection is definitively excluded -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 38-year-old woman with advanced HIV disease and ART interruption presenting with multiple cutaneous abscesses and draining sinuses

step5_concept_grounding: Advanced HIV disease with antiretroviral treatment interruption presenting with multiple cutaneous abscesses, cachexia, and recurrent tuberculosis

evidence_items.source_quote: A 38-year-old woman with advanced HIV disease (antiretroviral treatment experienced with treatment interruption) presented to Khayelitsha District Hospital with multiple cutaneous abscesses and associated constitutional symptoms of loss of appetite, loss of weight and night sweats.
evidence_items.test_name: Clinical history and documented advanced HIV disease

rationale: A 38-year-old woman with established advanced HIV disease and a history of antiretroviral treatment with subsequent treatment interruption presented with widespread cutaneous abscesses, discharging sinuses, weight loss, and fever. The patient had three previous treated episodes of drug-sensitive tuberculosis. The clinical presentation of advanced HIV disease with severe constitutional symptoms and opportunistic cutaneous manifestations establishes confirmed HIV infection. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Patient A: A 40-year-old male presenting with chronic cough, weight loss, and lymphadenopathy, diagnosed with retrovirus (HIV) infection and disseminated tuberculosis

step5_concept_grounding: Newly diagnosed human immunodeficiency virus (retrovirus) infection with profound CD4 lymphopenia (14 cells/mm3) and disseminated tuberculosis, successfully treated with HAART and anti-TB therapy

evidence_items.source_quote: He was then tested for retrovirus infection and was found to be positive. The CD4 cell count was 14 cells per millimeter squared.
evidence_items.test_name: Retrovirus (HIV) screening serology and CD4 cell count
evidence_items.target_concept: Retrovirus / HIV infection and CD4 T-cells

evidence_items.source_quote: The viral load was done 2 weeks back, and it was 800 copies, which is below the threshold for viral transmission (greater than 1000 copies).

rationale: A 40-year-old male presented with a one-month non-productive cough, marked weight loss, hepatosplenomegaly, and generalized lymphadenopathy. Diagnostic workup confirmed retroviral (HIV) infection with profound immunosuppression (CD4 count 14 cells/mm3) and disseminated tuberculosis (positive urine LAM, ultrasonographic hepatic/splenic micronodules, and FNAC of lymph nodes). He was initiated on anti-TB therapy followed by HAART (tenofovir + lamivudine + dolutegravir), resulting in clinical recovery and a follow-up viral load of 800 copies. Confirmatory testing and viral load monitoring confirm active HIV infection -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Patient B: A 27-year-old male partner-notified of HIV exposure, diagnosed with HIV/AIDS and subclinical tuberculosis

step5_concept_grounding: Newly diagnosed HIV/AIDS with profound CD4 lymphopenia (77 cells/mm3) and subclinical tuberculosis detected by urine LAM, initiated on HAART

evidence_items.source_quote: Patient B: The patient, a 27-year-old man, was just diagnosed with HIV/AIDS (3 months ago) after being tested for HIV serostatus following notification that his wife had tested positive for the virus at a nearby clinic.

Except for the CD4 count, which was determined to be 77cells/mm3, all baseline examinations, including tuberculosis investigations using a sputum gene expert, were non-revealing, and he subsequently tested for TB LAM, which yielded a positive result.

rationale: A 27-year-old man was diagnosed with HIV/AIDS following partner notification after his wife tested positive for HIV. Baseline laboratory assessment revealed severe CD4 depletion (77 cells/mm3) and positive urine TB LAM despite absent symptoms. He was commenced on anti-TB therapy followed by HAART (tenofovir + lamivudine + dolutegravir), which he tolerated well. Established diagnosis of HIV/AIDS with severe CD4 lymphopenia and HAART initiation satisfies clinical confirmation criteria -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Description of a multidisciplinary case care management team and operational model for HIV/AIDS patients; no individual human patient described

step5_concept_grounding: Operational protocol and multidisciplinary team management framework for HIV/AIDS care delivery
rationale: This text describes the composition and workflow of a multidisciplinary case care management team (case managers, AIDS specialists, nurses, psychologists, nutritionists) delivering outpatient and digital follow-up for patients starting antiviral therapy. It outlines clinical guidelines, WeChat messaging protocols, and staffing roles rather than reporting an individual patient's clinical encounter. Because there is no single identified human clinical patient (F2_SCOPE_COHORT), this case fails CCU criteria -> EXCLUDED_NON_SINGLE_PATIENT.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 48-year-old female with long-standing HIV on ART and stable schizophrenia presenting with psychotic relapse triggered by zidovudine-induced severe immunohemolytic anemia

step5_concept_grounding: Chronic well-controlled HIV infection on antiretroviral therapy (viral load <20 copies/mL) complicated by zidovudine-induced immunohemolytic anemia precipitating schizophrenia relapse

evidence_items.source_quote: Her medical history was significant for HIV infection, which was diagnosed in 2012.
In the past 3 yearly laboratory investigations, her CD4+ cell counts were between 1163-1935 cells/ul and viral loads were all < 20 copies/mL.
evidence_items.test_name: CD4 cell count and HIV RNA viral load
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV viral load and CD4 T-lymphocytes

rationale: A 48-year-old female diagnosed with HIV infection in 2012 and schizophrenia in 2014 presented with acute exacerbation of auditory hallucinations and severe anemia (hemoglobin 4.2 g/dL). Yearly laboratory investigations documented robust immune reconstitution (CD4 counts 1163-1935 cells/ul) and sustained virologic suppression (viral loads <20 copies/mL) on antiretroviral therapy. Her severe anemia was attributed to zidovudine and autoimmune hemolysis; replacement of zidovudine with tenofovir and blood transfusion led to rapid resolution of psychotic symptoms. Confirmed HIV infection on ART with documented viral load suppression establishes positivity -> POSITIVE.

rationale: A 6-year-old girl with congenital single kidney and chronic kidney disease on peritoneal dialysis developed aggressive gingival necrosis, alveolar bone destruction (osteomyelitis), and Pseudomonas aeruginosa septic shock. Surgical debridement and targeted antibiotic therapy resulted in clinical stabilization. At the six-month follow-up evaluation, diagnostic testing confirmed that human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) was detected despite previously negative serologic testing, explaining the severe necrotizing presentation. Confirmed detection of HIV in this pediatric patient establishes positive diagnosis -> POSITIVE.

Because this represents an aggregate health systems research study without an individual patient CCU (F2_SCOPE_COHORT), it is excluded -> EXCLUDED_NON_SINGLE_PATIENT.

was enrolled for HIV treatment/care and being followed up at the out patients  services.

She received acyclovir and antibiotics, achieved marked clinical recovery, and was enrolled in specialized HIV care and antiretroviral therapy. Positive confirmatory serology and documented CD4 lymphopenia satisfy criteria -> POSITIVE.

Documented enrollment in HIV services and initiation of ART in the setting of an AIDS-defining illness confirms HIV diagnosis -> POSITIVE.

Longstanding confirmed HIV infection monitored with serial CD4 counts and treated with ART establishes positivity -> POSITIVE.

rationale: A 23-year-old male with a verified 5-year history of HIV infection presented with decreased sleep, referential and persecutory delusions, and disorganized behavior, diagnosed with bipolar affective disorder (current episode mania with psychotic symptoms). step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 23-year-old male with HIV infection on combination antiretroviral therapy presenting with refractory severe psychotic depression induced by efavirenz

evidence_items.source_quote: In the meantime, he was tried with various antiretroviral drugs in combinations, i.e. lamivudine 150-300 mg, zidovudine 300 mg, nevirapine 600 mg, stavudine 20 mg, and tenofovir 300 mg.
Hence, he discontinued EFV and started nevirapine. After discontinuing EFV, the patient started to improve in a month and recovered completely in 3 months with good socio-occupational functioning.

rationale: This clinical case describes a patient with confirmed HIV infection who received sequential multi-agent antiretroviral therapy regimens (lamivudine, zidovudine, nevirapine, stavudine, tenofovir, and efavirenz). Following efavirenz prescription, he developed severe refractory psychotic depression (Beck Depression Inventory score of 55). Pharmacological discontinuation of efavirenz and substitution with nevirapine produced full psychological recovery within three months. Long-term multi-drug ART management in an established HIV patient confirms diagnosis -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 51-year-old female presenting as part of a family COVID-19 cluster, newly diagnosed with HIV-1 infection by Western blot and viral load PCR

evidence_items.target_concept: HIV-1 antibody Western blot and HIV-1 RNA

rationale: A 51-year-old female was admitted for COVID-19 pneumonia in a familial outbreak. Admission screening revealed positive HIV antibodies, confirmed by a definitive multi-band Western blot (gp160, gp120, p66, p55/51, gp41, p31, p24, p17) and an initial HIV-1 RNA viral load of 27,544 copies/mL. Combination ART (tenofovir, lamivudine, lopinavir/ritonavir) was instituted, resulting in viral load reduction to 1,723 copies/mL at 14 days and complete suppression to 0 copies/mL at 12 months. Gold-standard Western blot and quantitative RNA PCR establish confirmatory diagnosis -> POSITIVE.

rationale: A 45-year-old male presented with headache, fever, and vomiting, diagnosed with cryptococcal meningitis. Immunodeficiency evaluation showed a persistent CD4 lymphopenia (161-213 muL-1). Comprehensive investigation for HIV was negative/non-diagnostic, and extensive bone marrow, lymph node, cytogenetic, and immunological studies by the NIH excluded secondary immunodeficiencies. He was conclusively diagnosed with idiopathic CD4 lymphocytopenia (defined strictly by CD4 lymphopenia in the confirmed absence of HIV infection). Because HIV was evaluated and ruled out, this case is negative -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Primary subject of case report; 60-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis on adalimumab who acquired HIV

evidence_items.source_quote: Nonetheless, after RA was in control, HIV was detected in her blood, with a quantitative HIV-1 RNA test revealing values of 1.31E+5 IU/mL, accompanied by a decreased CD4+ lymphocyte count.

rationale: A 60-year-old female receiving adalimumab for difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis contracted HIV from a sexual partner. Routine monitoring revealed detectable HIV with a quantitative HIV-1 RNA viral load of 1.31 x 10^5 IU/mL and declining CD4+ lymphocyte counts. She initiated HAART alongside continued adalimumab, achieving viral replication control and immune recovery. E1 confirmatory lab establishes active HIV infection -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Primary subject of case report; 35-year-old female presenting with HIV-associated vacuolar myelopathy and dementia

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnosis of HIV infection presenting with HIV-associated vacuolar myelopathy and HIV-associated dementia (HAND)

evidence_items.source_quote: Then we sent for an HIV test, and it came as positive. Her absolute CD4 count was 54/microL.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV serological test and CD4 flow cytometry
evidence_items.result: HIV test POSITIVE, absolute CD4 count 54/microL

rationale: A 35-year-old female presented with progressive lower extremity paraparesis, oral thrush, cognitive impairment, and severe wasting. Diagnostic testing confirmed positive HIV status with an absolute CD4 count of 54 cells/microL, establishing HIV-associated vacuolar myelopathy and HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder. Initiation of HAART led to marked clinical and laboratory improvement. Highly specific clinical and laboratory findings confirm advanced HIV/AIDS -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Primary subject of case report; 64-year-old woman with squamous lung cancer and toxoplasmosis who tested negative for HIV

step5_concept_grounding: Evaluation for HIV infection in patient presenting with acute toxoplasmosis and lung cancer; test was negative

evidence_items.source_quote: Serology testing for HIV was negative.

rationale: A 64-year-old female was diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the right lung complicated by acute pulmonary toxoplasmosis detected in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. Because toxoplasmosis is an opportunistic infection classically associated with HIV/AIDS, serological testing for HIV was performed; serology testing for HIV was negative. Ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Primary subject of case report; 38-year-old male with retroviral infection on HAART presenting with leprosy IRIS

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnosis of retroviral (HIV) infection complicated by disseminated tuberculosis and leprosy immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome

evidence_items.source_quote: A 38-year-old male patient, diagnosed with retroviral infection and disseminated tuberculosis presented with weakness and numbness of the right hand of 2 weeks duration.

rationale: A 38-year-old male diagnosed with retroviral (HIV) infection and disseminated tuberculosis had been on ATT followed by HAART, with an initial CD4 count of 67 cells/microL. Five months into HAART, his CD4 count rose to 160 cells/microL and he developed borderline tuberculoid Hansen's disease presenting as an immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS). Established retroviral infection with characteristic IRIS recovery on HAART confirms HIV infection -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Primary subject of case report; 88-year-old male with HBV cirrhosis and primary effusion lymphoma who tested negative for HIV

step5_concept_grounding: Evaluation for HIV infection in patient presenting with primary effusion lymphoma; test was negative

evidence_items.source_quote: Anti-HIV: (-)

rationale: An 88-year-old male with HBV cirrhosis presented with ascites and was diagnosed with primary effusion lymphoma (PEL). Because PEL typically occurs in HIV-infected individuals, HIV serology was evaluated; the serological investigation revealed Anti-HIV: (-). Target disease is ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Primary subject of case 1; 49-year-old male with SLE and Talaromyces marneffei who tested negative for HIV

step5_concept_grounding: Evaluation for HIV infection in patient presenting with Talaromyces marneffei infection; test was negative

evidence_items.source_quote: Assessment for anti-nuclear antibody and anti-SS-A indicated positivity while anti-HIV antibody was not detected.

rationale: A 49-year-old male with systemic lupus erythematosus on prednisone presented with severe systemic Talaromyces marneffei infection. Because T. marneffei is predominantly an AIDS-associated mycosis in endemic regions, anti-HIV antibody testing was performed; anti-HIV antibody was not detected. Target disease is ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Primary subject of case 2; 27-year-old female with SLE and Talaromyces marneffei infection who tested negative for HIV

step5_concept_grounding: Evaluation for HIV infection in patient presenting with Talaromyces marneffei infection; test was negative

evidence_items.source_quote: Antinuclear antibodies were highly expressed (109.4 IU/mL), whereas anti-HIV antibodies were absent.

rationale: A 27-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus on long-term prednisone presented with thigh ulceration and septicemia caused by Talaromyces marneffei. Diagnostic assessment evaluated for underlying HIV infection given the typical association of talaromycosis with AIDS; anti-HIV antibodies were absent. Target disease is ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Multi-patient case series describing two clinical cases (Patient A and Patient B) of TDF PrEP failure in MSM

step5_concept_grounding: Case report describing failure of tenofovir disoproxil fumarate to prevent HIV acquisition across two patients

evidence_items.source_quote: Both patients had received TDF 300 mg/day for hepatitis B infection (hepatitis B s-antigen and e-antigen positive) and maintained a consistently undetectable hepatitis B DNA for 3+ years with no viral blips.
evidence_items.target_concept: Cohort of two MSM patients with HBV and acute HIV acquisition

rationale: This publication reports two distinct clinical cases (Patient A and Patient B) in a single narrative describing acute HIV infection acquired despite long-term tenofovir disoproxil fumarate treatment for hepatitis B. The document groups two independent patients into a single case unit without individual pair stratification. Excluded as multi-patient case series -> EXCLUDED_NON_SINGLE_PATIENT.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Primary subject of case report; 35-year-old Cameroonian female with AIDS (CDC stage C3) and opportunistic infections

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnosis of AIDS (CDC stage C3) complicated by duodenal histoplasmosis, cryptococcosis, and PML on cART

evidence_items.source_quote: A 35-year old Cameroonian female was diagnosed with AIDS (CDC stage C3) in May 2012.
evidence_items.test_name: Clinical diagnosis of CDC stage C3 AIDS

rationale: A 35-year-old female was diagnosed with AIDS (CDC stage C3) complicated by multiple opportunistic infections including duodenal histoplasmosis, cryptococcosis, and progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML). She received combination antiretroviral therapy (cART) that required regimen modification due to several HIV drug resistance mutations. Highly specific clinical evidence confirms advanced AIDS -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 37-year-old male with underlying HIV infection diagnosed in June 2015 presenting with acute renal failure secondary to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection complicated by profound CD4 lymphopenia and primary renal diffuse large B-cell lymphoma

evidence_items.source_quote: A 37-year-old gentleman with underlying human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) diagnosed in June 2015 was under infectious disease clinic follow-up from another center.
After 12 months of treatment, his HIV viral load was less than 20 cells/L, and CD4 increased to 178 cells/microliter and serum creatinine of 193 micromol/L.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV viral load and CD4 monitoring
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV viral load and CD4 count

evidence_items.source_quote: His repeat CD4 count was 84 cells/microliter, and the viral load was 6974 copies per ml.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV repeat CD4 and viral load
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV viral load and CD4 count

rationale: A 37-year-old male with HIV diagnosed in 2015 initially managed on tenofovir-emtricitabine and efavirenz defaulted treatment and presented with severe acute kidney injury, normocytic anemia, and retroperitoneal/renal diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. Serial quantitative HIV evaluation confirmed persistent infection with a repeat CD4 count of 84 cells/microliter and viral load of 6,974 copies/mL. Antiretroviral therapy (abacavir/lamivudine and efavirenz) was restarted with opportunistic infection prophylaxis. Conclusive quantitative laboratory evidence satisfies confirmatory criteria for HIV infection -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: An 18-year-old male presenting with acute CMV infection complicated by acute inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculopathy and splenic infarction; tested negative for HIV

step5_concept_grounding: Serological screening ruling out human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection in a patient presenting with CMV infection and Guillain-Barre syndrome

evidence_items.source_quote: Test for human immunodeficiency virus was negative.

rationale: An 18-year-old male presented with pharyngitis, malaise, hepatitis, acute inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculopathy, and subsequent splenic infarction associated with acute CMV viremia. During the diagnostic evaluation for potential underlying infectious and immunodeficiency etiologies, laboratory testing for human immunodeficiency virus was specifically performed and returned negative ('Test for human immunodeficiency virus was negative.'). Because HIV was specifically tested and ruled out by laboratory investigation, the case label is NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 28-year-old female presenting with disseminated Talaromyces marneffei and Mycobacterium fortuitum coinfection; tested negative on HIV serology

step5_concept_grounding: Serological screening ruling out human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection in an immunocompromised host presenting with opportunistic coinfection

evidence_items.source_quote: HIV serology and serum cryptococcal capsular antigen tests were negative.

rationale: A 28-year-old female presenting with cervical lymphadenopathy, recurrent fever, erythema nodosum, and lung infiltrates was found to have disseminated coinfection with Talaromyces marneffei and Mycobacterium fortuitum. Given the frequent occurrence of Talaromyces marneffei as an AIDS-defining opportunistic infection, diagnostic HIV serology was performed and confirmed to be negative ('HIV serology and serum cryptococcal capsular antigen tests were negative.'). Because HIV was formally tested and ruled out by serology, the case label is NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 34-year-old male with known HIV infection on tenofovir-lamivudine-dolutegravir ART, presenting with recurrent meningitis diagnosed as Streptococcus suis coinfection

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection with CD4 lymphopenia (171 cells/muL) on antiretroviral therapy, presenting with Streptococcus suis meningitis

evidence_items.source_quote: His medical history showed that he had had cryptococcal meningitis and HIV infection for about 1 year, and he had been receiving (with good compliance) fluconazole and tenofovir-lamivudine-dolutegravir based antiretroviral therapy (ART) during the same time period.
CD4 count 171 cells/muL; normal blood biochemical; negative 1,3-beta-D-glucan test (G test) and galactomannan test (GM test) results (0.1 mug/L).

rationale: A 34-year-old male with a documented 1-year history of HIV infection and prior cryptococcal meningitis maintained compliant on tenofovir-lamivudine-dolutegravir antiretroviral therapy presented with worsening headache and CD4 lymphopenia (171 cells/muL), diagnosed with Streptococcus suis meningitis by CSF metagenomic next-generation sequencing. Established HIV diagnosis actively treated with modern ART and accompanied by CD4 monitoring confirms the diagnosis -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 42-year-old male diagnosed with HIV in 1997, presenting in late-stage AIDS with CD4 count of 10 cells/mm3, giant perianal ulcer, and primary central nervous system lymphoma

step5_concept_grounding: Advanced human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) infection in AIDS stage with severe CD4 count depletion (10 cells/mm3), high viral load, and primary central nervous system lymphoma

evidence_items.source_quote: Medical history revealed that he was seropositive and diagnosed with HIV in 1997.
Four days later, on his 2nd visit, as per NACO, his HIV-1 status was confirmed by HIV-enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay.
His CD4 count (Absolute count and Percentage) was 10 cells/mm3, CD4-<4%, and plasma viral load was 43,803 copies/ml.
evidence_items.test_name: CD4 cell count and viral load
evidence_items.target_concept: CD4 count and HIV viral load

rationale: A 42-year-old male diagnosed with HIV in 1997 presented with fever, weight loss, oral candidiasis, and a large perianal ulcer, complicated by diffuse large B-cell primary central nervous system lymphoma. Confirmatory HIV-1 ELISA re-demonstrated seropositivity, and quantitative testing revealed profound immunosuppression (CD4 count 10 cells/mm3, CD4 <4%) and viral load of 43,803 copies/mL (subsequently 52,935 copies/mL). Antiretroviral resistance testing was performed and second-line ART instituted. Incontrovertible confirmatory ELISA, CD4 counts, and viral loads establish HIV infection -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 35-year-old female living with HIV on regular HAART, presenting with severe recurrent crusted hand and genital herpes simplex virus lesions

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection managed with HAART, presenting with recurrent severe mucocutaneous herpes simplex virus infection and CD4 count 236 cells/mm3

evidence_items.source_quote: She was diagnosed to be HIV positive 10 years ago and has been on regular "highly active antiretroviral treatment" since then.
Her CD4 count at the time of presentation to us was 236 cells/mm.

rationale: A 35-year-old female diagnosed with HIV 10 years prior and maintained on long-term highly active antiretroviral therapy presented with severe recurrent palm and genital lesions secondary to herpes simplex virus infection. Immunological evaluation confirmed a CD4 count of 236 cells/mm3. Confirmed HIV infection maintained on HAART with CD4 count monitoring satisfies criteria -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 30-year-old male presenting with porphyria cutanea tarda and newly diagnosed advanced HIV infection with CD4 count of 32 cells/mm3

step5_concept_grounding: Newly diagnosed human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection with severe CD4 lymphopenia (32 cells/mm3) presenting with porphyria cutanea tarda

evidence_items.source_quote: On serological testing, patient was found to be HIV positive with a CD4 count of 32 cells/mm3.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV serological test and CD4 count

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient was treated with low-dose hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice weekly, antiretroviral drugs and was advised photo protective measures.

rationale: A 30-year-old male presenting with photosensitive bullous lesions, facial hypertrichosis, and elevated urinary porphyrins was diagnosed with porphyria cutanea tarda. Diagnostic serological screening confirmed new HIV positivity with profound CD4 lymphopenia (32 cells/mm3). Antiretroviral therapy and low-dose hydroxychloroquine led to clinical resolution and CD4 cell reconstitution to 232 cells/mm3. Confirmatory serology and therapeutic response establish the diagnosis -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: An 18-year-old male with perinatal HIV infection treated since age 7, presenting with multi-class drug resistance including InSTI resistance mutations

step5_concept_grounding: Perinatally acquired human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection complicated by multi-class antiretroviral drug resistance mutations following treatment failure

evidence_items.source_quote: An 18-year-old male patient was commenced on ART in September 2010, at seven years of age. His baseline CD4 count was 145 cells/muL.
evidence_items.test_name: Pediatric ART initiation and CD4 nadir

evidence_items.source_quote: An HIV genotypic resistance test done in January 2015 showed significant nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) and non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI) DRMs with no protease inhibitor resistance (see Table 1 for DRMs and sensitivity results).

Despite adherence counselling his VL remained high, and an HIV genotypic resistance test taken 14 months after TDF/3TC/DTG initiation showed persistent NRTI and NNRTI DRMs, and extensive InSTI DRMs (see Table 1 for mutations and sensitivity analysis).

rationale: An 18-year-old male who initiated antiretroviral therapy for perinatally acquired HIV at age 7 experienced recurrent virological failures across successive regimens. Molecular genotypic drug resistance testing confirmed multi-class HIV-1 resistance mutations affecting NRTIs, NNRTIs, and integrase strand transfer inhibitors (InSTIs). Longstanding documented clinical care, viral load monitoring, and molecular sequencing of HIV-1 establish conclusive HIV infection -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 29-year-old female diagnosed with HIV in 2017 presenting with virological failure, viral load of 6540 copies/mL, and InSTI drug resistance while co-treated for tuberculosis

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection complicated by virological failure, tuberculosis coinfection, and integrase inhibitor resistance mutations

evidence_items.source_quote: A 29-year-old female patient was diagnosed with HIV infection in June 2017 and commenced on TDF/3TC/EFV.

A VL taken after seven months on ABC/3TC/DTG was 6540 copies/mL, despite adherence counselling. A genotypic resistance test taken 10 months after initiation of DTG showed extensive NRTI DRMs and one major InSTI DRM (see Table 1 for mutations and sensitivity analysis).
evidence_items.test_name: HIV viral load and genotypic resistance test
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV RNA PCR and drug resistance sequencing

rationale: A 29-year-old female diagnosed with HIV in 2017 developed virological failure during concurrent treatment for pulmonary tuberculosis. Laboratory evaluation demonstrated an elevated viral load of 6,540 copies/mL and genotypic resistance testing confirmed multiple HIV-1 drug-resistance mutations conferring resistance to NRTIs and dolutegravir. Quantitative viral load and molecular sequencing confirm HIV infection -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 36-year-old male presenting with chronic epididymitis secondary to Chlamydia trachomatis LGV-L2, tested negative for HIV

step5_concept_grounding: Laboratory testing ruling out human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection during STI panel evaluation for chronic epididymo-orchitis

evidence_items.source_quote: a panel of 17 sexually transmitted infections (STIs) including Human Immunodeficiency Virus, C. trachomatis, Ureaplasma urealyticum, Mycoplasma hominis, Mycoplasma genitalium, Herpes Simplex Virus type 1 and 2, Human Papilloma Virus, Trichomonas vaginalis, Treponema pallidum, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Escherichia coli, Pseudomonas spp., Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp. and Candida spp. were investigated by either PCR or culture as previously described.
evidence_items.test_name: STI panel PCR screening including HIV

evidence_items.source_quote: As shown in Table 1, a positive result was obtained for C. trachomatis infection while all the other pathogens were negative.

Overall, these results indicate that C. trachomatis LGV-L2 was identified as the cause of chronic epididymitis in an HIV-negative, heterosexual patient presenting without the typical LGV signs and symptoms.

rationale: A 36-year-old male presenting with chronic scrotal pain was evaluated with an extensive 17-pathogen sexually transmitted infection panel including Human Immunodeficiency Virus PCR. Molecular testing returned positive only for Chlamydia trachomatis (LGV L2) while HIV was confirmed negative, with the patient explicitly characterized as HIV-negative throughout the report. Because HIV was specifically tested and ruled out, the label is NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 55-year-old male presenting with classic Kaposi sarcoma of the lower extremities and soft palate; serologically negative for HIV

step5_concept_grounding: Serological testing ruling out human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) in a patient diagnosed with classic (non-epidemic) Kaposi sarcoma

evidence_items.source_quote: Serologic tests for HIV were negative, and the CD4 count was 350 cells/mm3 with a CD4/CD8 ratio of 1.10 and CD4% of 32%.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV serology and CD4/CD8 subset analysis

rationale: A 55-year-old male presenting with cutaneous nodular lesions and an oral palatal lesion was diagnosed with Kaposi sarcoma based on histopathology and HHV-8 positivity. Serologic testing for HIV was performed to exclude epidemic AIDS-related Kaposi sarcoma and was confirmed negative, with a normal CD4/CD8 ratio of 1.10, establishing classic (non-HIV-related) Kaposi sarcoma. Because HIV was tested and explicitly ruled out, the label is NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 38-year-old HIV-positive male not on antiretroviral therapy presenting with a right conjunctival mass diagnosed as leiomyosarcoma

step5_concept_grounding: Confirmed human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection in an untreated adult presenting with conjunctival leiomyosarcoma

evidence_items.source_quote: A 38-year-old HIV-positive male, who was not on antiretroviral treatment, presented with a right-sided conjunctival mass for an uncertain period of time.

rationale: A 38-year-old male with confirmed HIV infection not currently taking antiretroviral therapy presented with a conjunctival mass which on excision and immunohistochemical analysis was diagnosed as conjunctival leiomyosarcoma. The clinical report confirms the patient's HIV-positive status as a co-occurring condition. The case fulfills criteria for confirmed HIV presence -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 35-year-old male with follicular lymphoma in remission presenting with JC virus-induced progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy; confirmed HIV-negative

step5_concept_grounding: Clinical exclusion of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection in a patient developing progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy after rituximab therapy

evidence_items.source_quote: A 35-year-old HIV- (human immunodeficiency virus-) negative male presented with three weeks of right lower extremity paresthesias and right upper extremity apraxia.

rationale: A 35-year-old male in remission from follicular lymphoma developed subacute neurological deficits and was diagnosed with progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to JC virus. The patient was explicitly evaluated and documented as 'HIV- (human immunodeficiency virus-) negative'. The CCR5 antagonist maraviroc was administered as an experimental treatment for PML-IRIS rather than for HIV. Because HIV infection was specifically ruled out in this patient, the label is NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 29-year-old female with known HIV infection on HAART presenting with lactic acidosis secondary to plasmablastic lymphoma

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection established on highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART), complicated by plasmablastic lymphoma and lactic acidosis

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient is a 29-year-old female with a history of HIV on highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) who presented to the hospital with complaints of nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea.
The patient reported compliance with her HAART and denied recent changes to her regimen.

rationale: A 29-year-old female with confirmed HIV infection on compliant highly active antiretroviral therapy presented with severe lactic acidosis, marked lymphadenopathy, and hepatosplenomegaly diagnosed by lymph node biopsy as plasmablastic lymphoma. Her HAART regimen was evaluated and temporarily held during acute ICU management. Documented active HIV infection under continuous HAART management meets criteria for disease presence -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 34-year-old male presenting with microscopic hematuria, newly diagnosed with HIV infection (viral load 5.1x10^4/mm3, CD4 139 cells/muL), tubulointerstitial nephritis, and tuberculosis

step5_concept_grounding: Newly diagnosed human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection with severe CD4 lymphopenia (139 cells/muL) and high viral load, presenting with focal tubulointerstitial nephritis

evidence_items.source_quote: Upon initial routine workup, the patient's HIV test was positive. Subsequent blood tests showed CD4 count was 139 cells/muL and viral load was 5.1x104/mm3.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV diagnostic test and viral load/CD4 count
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV test, CD4 count, and viral load

evidence_items.source_quote: Two weeks after the initiation of treatment for tuberculosis, antiretroviral therapy (ART), including lamivudine, abacavir, and dolutegravir, was started.

rationale: A 34-year-old male evaluated for microscopic hematuria was found on screening to be HIV positive, with severe immunodeficiency (CD4 count 139 cells/muL) and high plasma viral load (5.1 x 10^4 copies/mm3). After diagnosing concurrent pulmonary tuberculosis, antiretroviral therapy consisting of lamivudine, abacavir, and dolutegravir was initiated, resulting in complete resolution of hematuria and normalization of renal tubular markers. Confirmatory serology and quantitative viral load establish HIV infection -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 53-year-old male with a history of HIV and hypertension presenting with recurrent primary cutaneous mucinous carcinoma of the right upper eyelid

step5_concept_grounding: Documented history of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection as a comorbid condition in a patient undergoing surgical resection of cutaneous mucinous carcinoma

evidence_items.source_quote: Past medical history was significant for hypertension and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).

rationale: A 53-year-old male with documented history of hypertension and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) presented with a recurrent right upper eyelid nodular lesion diagnosed as primary cutaneous mucinous carcinoma. The patient underwent wide local surgical excision and eyelid reconstruction. The case report documents confirmed history of HIV infection in an individual patient undergoing oncologic care -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 36-year-old male with known HIV infection restarting combination ART who developed immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) manifesting as rupioid secondary syphilis

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection managed with combination ART (elvitegravir, cobicistat, tenofovir, emtricitabine), complicated by immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) manifesting as rupioid secondary syphilis

evidence_items.source_quote: In late July, a 36-year-old African American man with a history of HIV and remote history of properly treated syphilis, presented to our institution for a second opinion regarding his recent diagnosis of peripheral T-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified (PTCL-NOS).

During the evaluation by his outside practitioner, he was told that his viral load was "very high", but uncertain in the number, though his CD4 count was 325 cells/ml. He was thus started on a combination of elvitegravir, cobicistat, tenofovir, and emtricitabine.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV viral load, CD4 count, and ART restart
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV viral load, CD4 count, combination ART

evidence_items.source_quote: In conjunction with the time course and increase in his CD4 count after starting ART, it was thought that his rupioid syphilis was derived from an immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS).

rationale: A 36-year-old male with a history of HIV infection and very high viral load resumed antiretroviral therapy with elvitegravir, cobicistat, tenofovir, and emtricitabine. Following ART reintroduction, his CD4 count rose from 325 to 450 cells/mL and he developed severe rupioid skin lesions consistent with secondary syphilis unmasked by immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS). Documented HIV infection with viral load, CD4 cell monitoring, and immune reconstitution satisfies confirmatory criteria -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 65-year-old male diagnosed with newly identified advanced HIV/AIDS (CD4 count 15 cells/muL, viral load >500,000 copies/mL) presenting with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia and CMV myeloradiculitis

step5_concept_grounding: Advanced human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection in AIDS stage (CD4 count 15 cells/muL, RNA >500,000 copies/mL) complicated by Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia and cytomegalovirus myeloradiculitis

evidence_items.source_quote: He was found to be HIV positive with a RNA level greater than 500,000 copies/ml and a CD4 count of 15.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV RNA viral load and CD4 count
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV-1 RNA viral load and CD4 count

evidence_items.source_quote: The serum HIV RNA PCR continued to decline and was 49 copies/mL on hospital day 128 (96 days after initiation of HAART therapy).
evidence_items.test_name: HIV RNA PCR virological response to HAART

rationale: A 65-year-old male presenting with respiratory failure was newly diagnosed with advanced HIV infection in the AIDS stage, confirmed by an HIV RNA viral load exceeding 500,000 copies/mL and a CD4 count of 15 cells/muL. He developed opportunistic coinfections including Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia and cytomegalovirus encephalitis/radiculomyelitis. HAART (elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, tenofovir alafenamide) achieved viral suppression down to 49 copies/mL. Definitive quantitative viral load and CD4 counts establish confirmed HIV/AIDS -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 59-year-old male with a 15-year history of HIV and recent viral load of 9340 copies/mL, non-compliant with ART, presenting with Clostridium paraputrificum bacteremia and cervical spine lesions

step5_concept_grounding: Chronic human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection with active viral replication (viral load 9340 copies/mL) presenting with Clostridium paraputrificum bacteremia

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient was a 59-year-old male from Dammam, Saudi Arabia with a history of HIV for 15 years, who was non-compliant to HIV treatment for five years.
The patient last visited the HIV clinic in December 2020 and blood tests showed a viral load of 9340 copies per mL.
The patient was prescribed tenofovir and emtricitabine; no antiretroviral resistance screening test was performed, and we could not obtain lymphocyte subset results.

rationale: A 59-year-old male with a 15-year history of HIV infection and documented viral non-suppression (viral load 9,340 copies/mL) due to treatment non-compliance presented with neck pain, neurological weakness, and Clostridium paraputrificum bacteremia. He was maintained on tenofovir and emtricitabine. Documented HIV infection with quantitative viral load and ART prescription confirms HIV infection -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 55-year-old female diagnosed with AIDS in 1999, who after discontinuing ART experienced severe multidermatomal herpes zoster with viral load 27,500 copies/mL and CD4 count 328 cells/mm3

step5_concept_grounding: Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) stage of HIV infection with viral rebound (27,500 copies/mL) and CD4 depletion following ART interruption, manifesting as aggressive herpes zoster

evidence_items.source_quote: A 55-year-old female patient of afro-descendant was diagnosed with AIDS in 1999, when she developed chronic diarrhea and weight loss.
Laboratory tests showed a normal complete blood count (CBC), a viral load (VL) of 27,500 copies/mL and a CD4+ T lymphocyte count of 328 cells/mm3.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV viral load and CD4 count
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV viral load and CD4 count

evidence_items.source_quote: She started therapy with AZT + lamivudine + abacavir.

rationale: A 55-year-old female diagnosed with AIDS in 1999 had interrupted antiretroviral treatment for 31 months, resulting in immunologic vulnerability and severe herpes zoster with neuralgia. Laboratory investigation demonstrated viral rebound with an HIV viral load of 27,500 copies/mL and CD4 count of 328 cells/mm3. Triple-combination ART (AZT + lamivudine + abacavir) was reinitiated with sustained clinical improvement. Established diagnosis of AIDS with quantitative viral load and CD4 count confirms the diagnosis -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Multicenter retrospective clinicopathological case series and systematic literature review of 53 cases of HIV-related CD8 encephalitis

step5_concept_grounding: Clinicopathological case series and review of CD8 encephalitis across adult HIV patient cohorts

evidence_items.source_quote: We reviewed cases of HIV-CD8E that were confirmed neuropathologically (on biopsy or at autopsy) in the UK between 2002 and February 2021.
