Extraction of the calculus by ureteroscopy was performed for FTIR constitutional analysis. Chronic HIV infection confirmed on active combination antiretroviral therapy satisfies diagnostic criteria -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A female patient with HIV infection and 10-year exposure to atazanavir/ritonavir presenting with atazanavir-induced urolithiasis confirmed by FTIR

step5_concept_grounding: Chronic HIV infection previously treated with protease inhibitor-based antiretroviral therapy (ritonavir-boosted atazanavir) presenting with atazanavir nephrolithiasis

evidence_items.source_quote: Our patient's medication history showed that ritonavir-boosted atazanavir (ATV/r) associated with tenofovir was carried on from 2007 to 2009.
In 2009, tenofovir was switched to abacavir, and association ATV/r with abacavir was given until 2017.

rationale: This clinical case segment details the compositional analysis of an obstructive urinary calculus in an HIV-infected patient, demonstrating by FTIR spectroscopy that the stone was predominantly composed of the antiretroviral protease inhibitor atazanavir (>70%). The patient's longitudinal antiretroviral history documented 10 consecutive years of treatment with ritonavir-boosted atazanavir (combined initially with tenofovir and subsequently with abacavir from 2007 to 2017). Established HIV infection treated with long-term antiretroviral therapy causing protease inhibitor urolithiasis satisfies diagnostic criteria -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: An 81-year-old female presenting with Bacillus cereus pneumonia and congestive heart failure, with incidental mention of absent HIV risk factors

step5_concept_grounding: Non-HIV case: elderly immunocompetent patient with Bacillus cereus pneumonia; HIV mentioned solely as an absent epidemiological risk factor

evidence_items.source_quote: She had no history of immunodeficiency, surgery, ill close contacts, risk factors for HIV or tuberculosis, recent central venous catheter insertion, or anthrax vaccination.
evidence_items.target_concept: Risk factors for HIV or tuberculosis

rationale: An 81-year-old woman was hospitalized with severe congestive heart failure and developed severe acute bilateral pneumonia with septicemia due to Bacillus cereus. The patient had no immunodeficiency, and the mention of HIV is limited to background anamnesis noting the absence of risk factors for HIV or tuberculosis (F5_DISCOURSE_CONTEXT). No HIV diagnostic testing or infection existed. Erroneous retrieval of a non-target condition -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 50-year-old female presenting with small bowel obstruction due to ileum histoplasmosis, who tested negative for HIV antibodies

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnostic exclusion of HIV infection via negative antibody testing in a patient presenting with intestinal obstruction from ileal histoplasmosis

evidence_items.source_quote: Furthermore, her HIV antibody test was negative.

rationale: A 50-year-old female presented with small bowel obstruction and severe localized fibrosis of the terminal ileum that was surgically resected and diagnosed as ileum histoplasmosis by senior pathology examination. Given the unusual presentation of localized gastrointestinal fungal infection, an HIV antibody test was performed and was explicitly negative. Confirmed absence of HIV infection by specific diagnostic laboratory testing -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 38-year-old man with an 8-year history of HIV-1 on cART undergoing targeted therapy for EGFR-mutant NSCLC who developed recurrent hypotensive shock from savolitinib

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) infection well-controlled on combination antiretroviral therapy (cART) with bictegravir, complicated by CD4 drop to <200 cells/muL during targeted cancer therapy

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient was a 38-year-old man with an 8-year history of HIV-1 positivity.
His initial combination antiviral therapy (cART) regimen was lamivudine plus efavirenz plus tenofovir, and the CD4+ cell count remained >500/microL after the regimen.
evidence_items.test_name: cART regimen history and CD4 count
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV cART response and CD4 count

evidence_items.source_quote: The cART regimen was eventually adjusted to bictegravir in January 2022, with good compliance.

rationale: A 38-year-old man with an 8-year history of HIV-1 infection managed with combination antiretroviral therapy (initially lamivudine/efavirenz/tenofovir, switched to bictegravir) was treated for metastatic EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer. During targeted therapy with savolitinib and almonertinib, he developed recurrent hypotensive shock and his CD4+ count dropped to <200 cells/muL. The patient has established HIV-1 infection on continuous cART, satisfying diagnostic criteria for confirmed HIV comorbidity. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 57-year-old male liver transplant recipient who developed donor-transmitted visceral leishmaniasis; HIV is mentioned strictly in background discussion of immunocompromising risk factors

step5_concept_grounding: Non-target case; discussion of visceral leishmaniasis risk factors in immunocompromised hosts, mentioning HIV as background epidemiological context

evidence_items.source_quote: Immunocompromise due to HIV, autoimmune disease, treatment with biological agents or other immunosuppression, and diabetes predisposes patients to more serious infections of VL.
evidence_items.test_name: Background review of immunocompromising risk factors

rationale: A 57-year-old man underwent orthotopic liver transplantation and developed donor-derived visceral leishmaniasis (Leishmania donovani complex) treated with liposomal amphotericin B. The patient's immunosuppression was due to post-transplantation pharmacotherapy (prednisolone, tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil). HIV is mentioned only once in the literature review section discussing general risk factors predisposing to serious Leishmania infections (F5_DISCOURSE_CONTEXT), without any clinical evaluation or diagnosis of HIV in the patient. Erroneous retrieval of a non-target condition -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 49-year-old African American female with untreated HIV infection presenting with VZV meningitis, optic neuritis, and progressive outer retinal necrosis (PORN) in the setting of uncontrolled AIDS

step5_concept_grounding: Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) stage of HIV infection with low CD4 count and high HIV viral load, complicated by opportunistic VZV meningitis, retrobulbar optic neuritis, and progressive outer retinal necrosis (PORN)

evidence_items.source_quote: A 49-year-old African American female patient with a history of untreated HIV infection presented to the emergency room with a two-week history of left ear pain, headache, fever, and blurred vision.
evidence_items.test_name: Clinical documentation of untreated HIV infection

evidence_items.source_quote: Laboratory assessment showed a low cluster of differentiation 4 (CD4) count and high HIV viral load consistent with uncontrolled AIDS (Table 1).
evidence_items.test_name: HIV viral load and CD4 count
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV viral load and CD4 count

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient responded well to the antiretroviral treatment, her CD4 count six months later was 317 cells/cubic milliliter, and her viral load decreased to 50 copies/ml.
evidence_items.test_name: Follow-up CD4 count and viral load response to ART
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV viral load and CD4 count

rationale: A 49-year-old woman with a history of untreated HIV infection presented with acute ophthalmic and central nervous system manifestations, including VZV meningitis, retrobulbar optic neuritis, and progressive outer retinal necrosis (PORN). Laboratory evaluation confirmed uncontrolled AIDS with a low CD4 count and elevated HIV viral load. Antiretroviral therapy (tenofovir, emtricitabine, boosted darunavir) was initiated alongside anti-VZV therapy, achieving viral suppression to 50 copies/mL and CD4 recovery to 317 cells/microL. Quantitative viral load and classic opportunistic infections confirm active HIV/AIDS. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 66-year-old male with past medical history of HIV, ESRD on hemodialysis, HTN, and T2D presenting with acute stroke-like symptoms and hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state in the setting of COVID-19

step5_concept_grounding: Past medical history of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection presenting with acute hyperglycemic hyperosmolar state, COVID-19, and stroke-like symptoms

evidence_items.source_quote: A 66-year-old male with a past medical history of hypertension (HTN), a prior cerebral vascular accident (CVA) without deficits, end-stage renal disease (ESRD) on hemodialysis, human immunovirus (HIV), and T2D presented to the ED for evaluation of stroke-like symptoms, in particular with newonset dysarthria and right facial droop.

rationale: A 66-year-old male with a documented medical history of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes presented with acute stroke-like symptoms and severe hyperglycemic hyperosmolar state alongside COVID-19 infection. The patient's established HIV infection is documented as a confirmed chronic comorbidity. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 53-year-old HIV-infected male on HAART (dolutegravir, emtricitabine/tenofovir) with undetectable HIV-1 RNA undergoing chemoradiotherapy, salvage surgery, and nivolumab immunotherapy for metastatic anal carcinoma

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) infection well-controlled on HAART with undetectable viral load, co-occurring with metastatic anal carcinoma treated with nivolumab

evidence_items.source_quote: A 53 years old HIV infected male patient was diagnosed with AC in September 2015. The patient had been diagnosed with HIV 6 years before, in 2009. At first presentation he was on highly active antiretroviral therapy with Dolutegravir and Emtricitabin/Tenofovir.
HIV 1-RNA has not been detectable during all treatment courses.

rationale: A 53-year-old male with HIV diagnosed in 2009 maintained on HAART (dolutegravir and emtricitabine/tenofovir) presented with locally advanced and subsequently metastatic anal carcinoma. He received chemoradiotherapy, salvage surgery, and successful immunotherapy with nivolumab. HIV-1 RNA was continuously monitored and remained undetectable throughout the course of antineoplastic therapy while CD4 counts were tracked. Documented long-term HIV infection on suppressive HAART with quantitative viral load monitoring confirms target disease comorbidity. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 53-year-old man presenting with chronic fever, diarrhea, and intestinal ulcers diagnosed with Talaromyces marneffei opportunistic infection in the setting of newly diagnosed advanced HIV infection with CD4 10 cells/mul

step5_concept_grounding: Newly diagnosed human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection in AIDS stage with profound CD4 T-cell lymphopenia (10 cells/mul) complicated by gastrointestinal Talaromyces marneffei infection

evidence_items.source_quote: Anti-HIV antibody was positive, and the patient's CD4 T count was 10 cells/mul, accounting for 2.16% of total T lymphocytes.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV antibody serology and CD4 T-cell count
evidence_items.target_concept: Anti-HIV antibody and CD4 T lymphocytes

rationale: A 53-year-old man presented with fever, diarrhea, weight loss, and multiple colonic ulcers. Laboratory workup revealed positive anti-HIV antibody and severe CD4 T-cell lymphopenia (10 cells/mul, 2.16% of total T lymphocytes), establishing newly diagnosed late-stage HIV/AIDS. Histopathology and fungal stains confirmed disseminated Talaromyces marneffei infection. Positive HIV serology with profound CD4 immunodeficiency in the setting of an AIDS-defining opportunistic mycosis provides conclusive confirmatory evidence. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 32-year-old HIV-1-infected widow on HAART presenting with severe AIDS wasting syndrome, diarrhea, oral thrush, and profound CD4 depletion (34 cells/ul) successfully treated with nutritional rehabilitation and ART switch

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) infection in AIDS stage with severe wasting syndrome, persistent high viral load (41,000 copies/ml), and profound CD4 depletion (34 cells/ul)

evidence_items.source_quote: A 32-year-old HIV-1-infected widow was admitted to our tertiary hospital with a 6-month history of progressive lethargy, anorexia, recurrent fever, vomiting, watery non-bloody diarrhoea, and progressive weight loss.

She was on HAART (Zidovudine, Lamivudine, Nevirapine) for 16 months but adherence was poor (<70%). On HAART, her viral reduced from 421,000 copies/ml to 41,000 copies/ml, but CD4+ T cell count dropped from 168 cells/ul to 34 cells/ul.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV viral load and CD4 count on HAART
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV-1 viral load and CD4 T-cell count

rationale: A 32-year-old HIV-1-infected woman on HAART presented with severe AIDS wasting syndrome (kwashiorkor-like malnutrition, 42% body weight loss) and oral candidiasis. Laboratory evaluation documented virological failure with an HIV viral load of 41,000 copies/mL and profound CD4 T-cell lymphopenia (34 cells/uL) due to suboptimal treatment adherence. She was managed with intensive nutritional rehabilitation and an ART regimen switch to emtricitabine/tenofovir and nevirapine. Confirmed viral load and CD4 count depletion satisfy confirmatory laboratory criteria. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 44-year-old woman with multicentric Castleman disease and chronic myelomonocytic leukemia, confirmed negative for HIV and HHV-8

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnostic rule-out of HIV infection in an adult female presenting with multicentric Castleman disease and chronic myelomonocytic leukemia

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient's serum tested negative for HIV, and no cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, or human herpes virus-8 (HHV-8) replication was detected.
She was diagnosed with HIV-negative and HHV-8-negative multicentric Castleman disease of plasma cell variant.

rationale: A 44-year-old woman presenting with cough, asthenia, generalized lymphadenopathy, and splenomegaly was diagnosed with multicentric Castleman disease (plasma cell variant) and chronic myelomonocytic leukemia. Diagnostic infectious workup specifically tested her serum for HIV, which was negative ('The patient's serum tested negative for HIV'). Because HIV was formally evaluated and confirmed absent by laboratory serology, the label is NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A group of 4 patients aged 50, 52, 57, and 75 years old with long histories of HIV-1 infection and thymidine analogue resistance mutations switched to RPV/DTG

step5_concept_grounding: Aggregate clinical summary of four patients with multi-drug resistant HIV-1 undergoing regimen optimization to rilpivirine and dolutegravir

evidence_items.source_quote: These 4 patients were 50, 52, 57, and 75 years old, respectively, who had a long history of HIV-1 infection and multiple treatments with several regimens.

rationale: This clinical vignette summarizes a group of 4 patients aged 50, 52, 57, and 75 years old with long-standing HIV-1 infection and thymidine analogue mutations who were switched to RPV/DTG. Because it summarizes multiple patients in aggregate rather than detailing an individual patient clinical care encounter (F2_SCOPE_COHORT), the case is excluded -> EXCLUDED_NON_SINGLE_PATIENT.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 55-year-old male with 20-year history of HIV-1 treatment, high cardiovascular risk, and renal impairment switched to RPV/DTG

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) infection on long-term antiretroviral therapy (20 years) optimized to rilpivirine/dolutegravir due to renal failure and cardiovascular comorbidities

evidence_items.source_quote: A 55-year-old male, with 20 years history of HIV-1 treatment, did not experience any virological failures; therefore, no GRT was performed.

Optimization to RPV/DTG was aimed at reducing pill burden, maintaining the advantage of a kidney-friendly regimen, thus not needing renal adjustment in case of glomerular filtration rate decline below 50 mL/min.

rationale: A 55-year-old male with a 20-year history of antiretroviral treatment for HIV-1 without virological failures required regimen optimization due to renal impairment and high cardiovascular risk. He was successfully transitioned to a two-drug regimen of rilpivirine and dolutegravir (RPV/DTG) to avoid renal toxicity. The patient has established HIV-1 infection with 20 years of continuous antiretroviral treatment, fulfilling clinical criteria for confirmed target disease. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 48-year-old male with 16-year history of HIV-1 infection with NRTI and NNRTI resistance mutations optimized to RPV/DTG

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) infection with documented resistance mutations to NRTI, efavirenz, and nevirapine undergoing regimen optimization to rilpivirine and dolutegravir

evidence_items.source_quote: A 48-year-old male, with 16 years of infection, acquired HIV-1 virus with associated resistance mutations to NRTI, efavirenz, and nevirapine with complete susceptibility to ETR.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV-1 infection and resistance genotyping history

evidence_items.source_quote: Optimization to RPV/DTG was aimed to reduce pill burden.

rationale: A 48-year-old male with a 16-year history of HIV-1 infection had documented viral resistance mutations conferring resistance to NRTIs, efavirenz, and nevirapine with susceptibility to etravirine. Treatment was optimized to rilpivirine and dolutegravir (RPV/DTG) to reduce pill burden. Confirmed genotypic resistance testing and multi-year antiretroviral management substantiate confirmed HIV-1 infection. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 29-year-old female with perinatally acquired HIV-1 and A98G resistance substitution successfully simplified to RPV/DTG

step5_concept_grounding: Perinatally acquired human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) infection with A98G resistance substitution on simplified maintenance therapy with rilpivirine and dolutegravir

evidence_items.source_quote: A 29-year-old female with mother-to-child transmission of HIV-1 has a peculiar pattern of resistance, with A98G substitution, that has a debated role in conferring a low-level resistance to RPV, thus not relevant according to IAS-USA Drug Resistance Mutations Group.
evidence_items.test_name: Mother-to-child HIV transmission and genotypic resistance

evidence_items.source_quote: Treatment with ETV was started in order to avoid ritonavir-related toxicity and then successfully simplified to RPV/DTG.

rationale: A 29-year-old woman with vertically acquired HIV-1 infection had a documented A98G reverse transcriptase substitution. She was initially treated with etravirine to prevent ritonavir-related toxicity and subsequently simplified to dual therapy with rilpivirine and dolutegravir (RPV/DTG). Documented mother-to-child transmission, genotypic resistance profile, and long-term antiretroviral therapy confirm target disease diagnosis. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 35-year-old man diagnosed with HIV 2 months prior on ART presenting with secondary syphilis rash and alopecia

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection diagnosed two months prior with established antiretroviral therapy, presenting with co-occurring psoriasiform secondary syphilis

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient was diagnosed with HIV two months prior to admission and had been on antiretroviral therapy (ART).
evidence_items.test_name: HIV diagnosis and ART initiation history

evidence_items.source_quote: The ART was planned to be resumed.

rationale: A 35-year-old man presented with widespread scaly plaques and alopecia diagnosed as psoriasiform secondary syphilis. He was diagnosed with HIV two months prior to admission and had been initiated on antiretroviral therapy (temporarily held for suspected drug rash). Treatment with benzathine penicillin resolved the syphilis lesions, and ART was scheduled for resumption. Established diagnosis of HIV on antiretroviral therapy confirms target disease comorbidity. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 50-year-old male with HIV, ESRD on peritoneal dialysis, and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma presenting with serpentine supravenous hyperpigmentation following R-CHOP chemotherapy

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection in an adult male undergoing R-CHOP chemotherapy for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma

evidence_items.source_quote: A 50-year-old male with HIV, ESRD on PD, HTN, and recently diagnosed DLBCL presented to the Emergency Department with RUE pain and swelling ten days after receiving his first cycle of R-CHOP (cyclophosphamide dose reduced for PD) through a peripheral IV in the right hand.

rationale: A 50-year-old man with HIV, ESRD on peritoneal dialysis, and hypertension presented ten days after his first cycle of R-CHOP chemotherapy for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with arm pain and vein hyperpigmentation diagnosed as serpentine supravenous hyperpigmentation. HIV infection is documented as a known chronic comorbid diagnosis in a patient undergoing antineoplastic therapy. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Cohort of 501 MSM participants in San Francisco enrolled in the I-TRIP respondent-driven sampling recruitment methodology study

step5_concept_grounding: Epidemiological and recruitment study of an aggregate cohort of 501 MSM participants assessing HIV status and peer referral networks

evidence_items.source_quote: A total of 501 participants were enrolled in the I-TRIP study.
evidence_items.test_name: Study cohort enrollment and sample size

evidence_items.source_quote: Participants were mostly white (n = 326), residents of San Francisco (n = 425), self-identified as homosexual or gay (n = 479), HIV-negative (n = 370) and had a college degree or higher (n = 418).
evidence_items.test_name: Aggregate cohort demographic and HIV status distribution

rationale: This publication reports findings from the I-TRIP study evaluating respondent-driven sampling recruitment among 501 MSM participants in San Francisco. It analyzes recruitment network profiles, return rates, and aggregate demographic and HIV characteristics rather than an individual patient clinical care episode (F2_SCOPE_COHORT). Because this is an aggregate population cohort study, it is excluded -> EXCLUDED_NON_SINGLE_PATIENT.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 42-year-old HIV-positive female on HAART with CD4 count of 374 cells/mm3 presenting with recurrent Kaposi sarcoma manifesting as breast and musculoskeletal masses

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection controlled on HAART (undetectable viral load, CD4 374 cells/mm3) presenting with recurrent extracutaneous Kaposi sarcoma of the breast and lower back

evidence_items.source_quote: A 42-year-old HIV-positive woman with a CD4 count of 374 cell/mm3 and an HIV viral load lower than detectable, presented to mammography with masses in the left breast and lower back.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV serostatus, CD4 count, and viral load
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV status, CD4 count, and HIV viral load

evidence_items.source_quote: She was on highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) since her previous presentation.

rationale: A 42-year-old HIV-positive woman on HAART with a CD4 count of 374 cells/mm3 and undetectable HIV viral load presented with palpable masses in the left breast and lower back. Biopsy and immunohistochemistry (positive for HHV-8) confirmed recurrent Kaposi sarcoma invading muscle and adjacent ribs. Documented HIV infection with laboratory viral load monitoring and ongoing HAART in the context of an AIDS-defining malignancy confirms target disease diagnosis. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 61-year-old Hispanic male presenting with abdominal pain, weight loss, and septic shock, newly diagnosed with HIV-1 infection (viral load 309,000, CD4 38) complicated by fatal disseminated coccidioidomycosis

step5_concept_grounding: Newly diagnosed human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) infection in AIDS stage with CD4 count of 38 cells/mm3 and plasma viral load of 309,000 copies/mL, complicated by fatal disseminated coccidioidomycosis

evidence_items.source_quote: Further testing showed that he was positive for HIV-1 with viral load 309,000 and CD4 count 38.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV-1 confirmatory testing, viral load, and CD4 count
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV-1 RNA viral load and CD4 count

evidence_items.source_quote: The cause of death was acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) secondary to disseminated coccidioidomycosis secondary to HIV/AIDS infection.
evidence_items.test_name: Autopsy diagnosis and cause of death

rationale: A 61-year-old man presented with abdominal pain, profound weight loss, generalized lymphadenopathy, and septic shock. Hospital workup confirmed he was positive for HIV-1 with an elevated viral load of 309,000 copies/mL and severe CD4 depletion (38 cells/mm3). Despite resuscitation, the patient died, and autopsy confirmed disseminated coccidioidomycosis with miliary pulmonary spread secondary to advanced HIV/AIDS infection. Quantitative viral load and CD4 count confirm active target disease. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 39-year-old HIV-positive female with AIDS diagnosed 7 years prior presenting with severe pandemic (H1N1) 2009 pneumonia resulting in multiorgan failure and death

step5_concept_grounding: Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) diagnosed 7 years prior with CD4 count of 166 cells/muL, complicated by fatal pandemic influenza A (H1N1) 2009 pneumonia

evidence_items.source_quote: We report pneumonia associated with pandemic (H1N1) 2009, which resulted in respiratory and renal failure and death, in a 39-year-old HIV-positive woman. She had type 1 diabetes and a diagnosis of AIDS 7 years ago and had received highly active antiretroviral therapy.
Her most recent CD4 cell count was 166 cells/muL with undetectable viral load 1 month before admission.
evidence_items.test_name: CD4 cell count and viral load monitoring
evidence_items.target_concept: CD4 cell count and HIV viral load

rationale: A 39-year-old woman with a 7-year diagnosis of AIDS and history of opportunistic Nocardia infection presented with severe community-acquired pneumonia and multiorgan failure secondary to pandemic influenza A (H1N1) 2009. Prior to admission, her CD4 cell count was 166 cells/muL with undetectable viral load on antiretroviral therapy. Despite intensive care and oseltamivir, she died on hospital day 11. Documented AIDS diagnosis, prior opportunistic infections, CD4 lymphopenia, and HAART history confirm target disease comorbidity. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 13-year-old male with vertically acquired HIV and multi-class drug resistance (M184V, INSTI mutations conferring high-level dolutegravir resistance) switched to darunavir-based third-line ART

step5_concept_grounding: Vertically acquired human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection with recurrent virological failure and multi-class resistance mutations (M184V and INSTI resistance mutations T66TI, G118R, E138K)

evidence_items.source_quote: Our index case is a 13-year-old male from a rural area in who acquired HIV through vertical transmission.
Figure 1 shows the HIV viral load (VL) and CD4 count timeline after ART initiation with no evidence of viral suppression defined as < 50 copies/mL.
evidence_items.test_name: Longitudinal HIV viral load and CD4 monitoring
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV viral load and CD4 count timeline

evidence_items.source_quote: Due to poor adherence and patient not suppressing for two years on the DTG-based regimen, despite enhanced adherence counselling, HIV DR was done in April 2022 which showed M184V again and the development of InSTI mutations (major T66TI, G118R, E138K, minor M50I), conferring high-level resistance to DTG (refer to Table 1).

rationale: A 13-year-old male with vertically acquired HIV infection diagnosed in 2010 experienced persistent virological failure on multiple lines of ART due to social vulnerabilities and adherence challenges. Longitudinal viral load tracking demonstrated unsuppressed viremia (>1000 copies/mL). HIV drug resistance genotyping in 2022 revealed the M184V mutation and major integrase strand transfer inhibitor (InSTI) resistance mutations (T66TI, G118R, E138K), conferring high-level resistance to dolutegravir, prompting a switch to third-line therapy with darunavir. Confirmatory longitudinal viral loads and resistance genotyping establish confirmed HIV infection. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 20-year-old male presenting with cervical and occipital lymphadenopathy diagnosed with acute toxoplasmosis; HIV antibody ELISA negative

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnostic rule-out of HIV infection in an immunocompetent young adult male presenting with lymphadenopathy secondary to acute toxoplasmosis

evidence_items.source_quote: An HIV antibody enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) test was also negative.

rationale: A 20-year-old man presented with persistent cervical, occipital, and inguinal lymphadenopathy after ingesting raw kibbe, ultimately diagnosed with acute toxoplasmosis. As part of the initial infectious and lymphadenopathy diagnostic workup, an HIV antibody ELISA was performed and was explicitly negative ('An HIV antibody enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) test was also negative'). Because HIV was directly tested and ruled out by confirmatory laboratory serology, the label is NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 38-year-old HIV-positive male with CD4 count of 94 cells/cu. mm and viral load of 107,400 copies/mL developing unmasking lepromatous leprosy and ENL as immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) after starting ART

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) infection with severe baseline CD4 lymphopenia (94 cells/cu. mm) and high viral load (107,400 copies/mL) presenting with leprosy-associated immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS)

evidence_items.source_quote: A 38-year-old male, diagnosed as HIV-positive, presented to our department with multiple painful, erythematous skin lesions over extremities, face and abdomen of 2 days duration along with the history of evening rise of temperature with chills, malaise, body pains, joint pains, and ankle edema.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV-positive clinical presentation and ART history

evidence_items.source_quote: HIV-1 was reactive, the viral load was 1,07,400 copies/mL and CD4 count 94 cells/cu. mm before starting ART.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV-1 serology, viral load, and CD4 count
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV-1 serology, viral load, and CD4 count

evidence_items.source_quote: On the basis of the history, clinical examination, and investigative findings, a diagnosis of IRIS presenting as ENL in a patient of HIV with unmasking of lepromatous leprosy was made.
evidence_items.test_name: Diagnosis of leprosy-associated IRIS in HIV

rationale: A 38-year-old man with advanced HIV-1 infection (baseline viral load 107,400 copies/mL, CD4 count 94 cells/cu. mm) initiated antiretroviral therapy (zidovudine, lamivudine, nevirapine). One month later, as CD4 counts rose to 151 cells/cu. mm, he developed tender subcutaneous nodules and nerve thickening diagnosed as erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL) and lepromatous leprosy representing immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS). Positive HIV-1 serology, quantitative viral load, and CD4 nadir below 100 cells/cu. mm provide conclusive E1 laboratory evidence of active HIV infection. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 69-year-old male with history of HIV infection and CD4 count of 319 presenting with gastrointestinal bleeding, esophageal candidiasis, and Empedobacter brevis bacteremia

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection with CD4 count of 319 cells/muL, complicated by opportunistic esophageal candidiasis and Empedobacter brevis bacteremia

evidence_items.source_quote: A 69-year-old Panamanian man with history of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection with CD4 count of 319 presented from a long term facility with chief complaint of black tarry stools for 2 days associated with malaise, nausea, and vomiting for one week.

evidence_items.source_quote: The antigen/antibody test for the human immunodeficiency virus was negative, while Chest CT showed no abnormalities.

On the 6th day, 2 mL of CSF was collected and analyzed for the presence of HIV RNA qPCR 910 copies/mL, and blood HIV RNA qPCR 1.37x10^5 copies/mL (Figure 3).

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 58-year-old male presenting with headache, gait apraxia, recent memory loss, and weight loss, diagnosed with HIV and cerebral toxoplasmosis

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 48-year-old Chinese male presenting with facial and trunk eruptions diagnosed as eosinophilic pustular folliculitis associated with secondary syphilis, with negative HIV testing

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 31-year-old Chinese male presenting with erythrodermic psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis, newly diagnosed with HIV infection with severe CD4 depletion

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 29-year-old female with chronic psychosis presenting with neuroleptic malignant syndrome, found to be HIV-positive by ELISA

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 33-year-old Caucasian male with advanced AIDS, CD4 count 59 cells/mm3, and HIV-1 RNA 308,000 copies/mL presenting with disseminated histoplasmosis and MAC

Established HIV infection with documented opportunistic AIDS illnesses and viral suppression confirms disease presence -> POSITIVE.

rationale: A female child born in May 1999 was diagnosed with HIV-1 in January 2002 as the index case in her family. Conclusive quantitative HIV RNA viral load confirms diagnosis -> POSITIVE.

rationale: A 73-year-old male presented with cavitary lung lesions found to represent co-existing pulmonary cryptococcosis and squamous cell carcinoma. Because he was found to have marked CD4+ T-lymphocytopenia (127 x 106/L), comprehensive evaluation for HIV infection was performed. HIV antibodies were confirmed negative by both ELISA and Western blot, and HIV p24 antigen was undetectable, with repeat testing at 10 months remaining negative (establishing idiopathic CD4 lymphopenia). Conclusive negative laboratory testing confirms absence of HIV infection -> NEGATIVE.

rationale: A 51-year-old woman with known HIV infection diagnosed 2 years prior on combination antiretroviral therapy (lamivudine, zidovudine, lopinavir/ritonavir) and TMP/SMX prophylaxis, with recent CD4 count of 220 cells/uL, presented with respiratory symptoms and bilateral cavitating pulmonary nodules. Percutaneous core needle biopsy of the cavitary lesion demonstrated granulomatous inflammation containing Pneumocystis jirovecii on methenamine silver staining. Treatment with therapeutic TMP/SMX led to clinical resolution. Established HIV infection managed with active combination ART satisfies disease criteria -> POSITIVE.

rationale: A 37-year-old male presenting with unilateral blurred vision, left sensorineural hearing loss, and a generalized macular rash was diagnosed with secondary syphilis with otic and optic involvement. Intravenous and intramuscular penicillin therapy resolved visual and auditory deficits. Conclusive molecular viral load quantification confirms active HIV infection -> POSITIVE.

rationale: A 42-year-old male with known HIV seropositivity presented with fever, sore throat, diarrhea, and pulmonary micronodules. Immunological testing revealed profound immunosuppression with a peripheral CD4+ T lymphocyte count of 25 cells/uL. Bronchial washings and blood cultures confirmed disseminated Penicillium marneffei (Talaromyces marneffei) infection via cytology, culture, and PCR. Treatment with amphotericin B followed by oral itraconazole produced marked improvement. Established HIV infection with profound CD4 count depletion and classic AIDS-defining opportunistic mycosis satisfies diagnostic criteria -> POSITIVE.

rationale: A 29-year-old Hispanic male with established HIV infection for 6 years on HAART therapy presented with rapid unilateral vision loss. Laboratory records documented persistent immunodeficiency (CD4 count of 100 cells/uL) and detectable HIV RNA viral load of 617 copies/mL. Biopsy of a retrobulbar orbital mass revealed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (CD10+, CD20+, BCL-2+, BCL-6+, Ki-67 >90%), an AIDS-defining malignancy. Quantifiable viral load and chronic management with HAART confirm HIV infection -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 30-year-old Chinese female presenting with fever, cough, pulmonary lesions, and osteolytic thoracic spine lesions from Talaromyces marneffei with high-titer anti-IFN-gamma autoantibodies; HIV test was negative

rationale: A 30-year-old female presented with persistent fever, cough, and thoracic back pain unresponsive to conventional antibiotics and empirical anti-tuberculosis therapy. Diagnostic evaluation for underlying immunodeficiency confirmed that the HIV test was negative. Metagenomic NGS and PCR confirmed disseminated Talaromyces marneffei pneumonia and spondylitis, with subsequent ELISA demonstrating high titers of anti-interferon-gamma autoantibodies (1:2500), defining adult-onset immunodeficiency in an HIV-uninfected host. Because HIV was tested and ruled absent, the case is classified as NEGATIVE.

rationale: A 27-year-old albino woman presented with a rapidly enlarging temporoparietal scalp mass confirmed histologically as Merkel cell carcinoma alongside cutaneous squamous cell carcinomas. Laboratory investigations confirmed HIV infection with low CD4+ cell count of 109 cells/uL and a quantitative HIV viral load of 640 RNA copies/mL. HAART was initiated alongside surgical and oncological management. Conclusive laboratory confirmation with quantitative viral load and initiation of antiretroviral therapy satisfies diagnostic criteria -> POSITIVE.

Documented HIV infection with quantitative viral monitoring and long-term ART management satisfies disease presence criteria -> POSITIVE.

Stool examination confirmed Cryptosporidium parvum oocysts, which resolved with nitazoxanide. Because HIV was evaluated and confirmed absent by serology, the case is classified as NEGATIVE.

rationale: A 36-year-old male with an established history of HIV and AIDS nonadherent to HAART presented with acute encephalopathy and fever. Diagnostic workup showed positive serum cryptococcal antigen and blood cultures growing Cryptococcus neoformans, confirming disseminated cryptococcemia and cryptococcal meningitis. The patient rapidly deteriorated with elevated intracranial pressure, brain herniation, and brain death. Documented history of AIDS with poor adherence to HAART and classic AIDS-defining opportunistic cryptococcal meningoencephalitis satisfies confirmatory criteria -> POSITIVE.

The excerpt presents composite illustrative vignettes (Box 1: Benta and her 2-year-old child, who left hospital without HIV testing; Box 2: Paul, a transgender youth tested without consent) alongside broad commentary on key populations. The document does not represent a primary clinical case report detailing an individual patient encounter (F2_SCOPE_COHORT). The case fails single patient CCU criteria -> EXCLUDED_NON_SINGLE_PATIENT.

rationale: A 32-year-old woman presented with umbilicated skin lesions in an academic case series on HIV-associated infectious diseases. Laboratory evaluation revealed a profound CD4 T-cell depletion to 1 cell/microL, accompanied by positive serum and CSF cryptococcal latex antigen and CSF culture confirmation of Cryptococcus neoformans. Disseminated cryptococcosis in conjunction with near-total CD4 count depletion (1 cell/microL) represents end-stage AIDS immunodeficiency in this clinical series. Meets diagnostic criteria -> POSITIVE.

Disseminated MAC in an HIV-positive patient is a definitive AIDS-defining condition. Established HIV infection with confirmed opportunistic infection satisfies diagnostic criteria -> POSITIVE.

rationale: A 34-year-old male receiving antiretroviral therapy presented with a fungating lesion on his right foot. Immunological testing documented severe immunosuppression with a CD4 count of 21 cells/microL. Biopsy revealed vascular proliferation with plump endothelial cells, and Warthin-Starry staining confirmed clumps of Bartonella bacilli consistent with bacillary angiomatosis, an opportunistic vascular infection characteristically seen in advanced HIV. Confirmed HIV on active ART with profound CD4 depletion meets diagnostic criteria -> POSITIVE.

Laboratory testing documented a CD4 count of 219 cells/microL, and diagnostic workup including skin biopsy immunohistochemistry and serology (reactive RPR titer 1:1024, positive T. pallidum antibody) confirmed secondary syphilis in the context of immune reconstitution on ART. Established HIV infection treated with antiretroviral therapy satisfies diagnostic criteria -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 32-year-old woman with profound CD4 lymphopenia (18 cells/microL) presenting with dual HSV and CMV perianal ulceration in an HIV-associated infectious disease series

Confirmed HIV infection with severe immunodeficiency satisfies criteria -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 40-year-old female with known HIV/AIDS for 14 years on ART successfully switched to third-line regimen (TLD+DRV/r) achieving virological suppression and CD4 recovery to 950 cells/mm3

rationale: A 40-year-old female known HIV/AIDS patient with a 14-year history of antiretroviral therapy presented with second-line virological and immunological failure (viral load 98,136 copies/mL, CD4 15 cells/mm3) complicated by severe pancytopenia and Cryptosporidium parvum enteritis. step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 32-year-old African American male presenting with abdominal pain and secondary syphilis, newly diagnosed with HIV-1 infection (viral load 115,000 copies/mL)

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) infection presenting concurrently with secondary syphilis and syphilitic hepatitis

evidence_items.source_quote: Furthermore, his HIV screen was positive with a HIV-1 viral load of 115,000 copies/mL and CD4+ cell count of 598 mm3. He was started on antiretroviral treatment and a lumbar puncture (LP) was performed.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV screen, HIV-1 viral load PCR, and CD4 count
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV-1 viral load and CD4 count

rationale: A 32-year-old male presented with abdominal pain, palmar and plantar maculopapular rash, and cholestatic transaminitis diagnosed as secondary syphilis. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 17-year-old male presenting with chest pain, fever, and severe odynophagia diagnosed with herpes simplex esophagitis, screened negative for HIV

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnostic exclusion of HIV infection in an immunocompetent adolescent presenting with herpes simplex virus esophagitis

evidence_items.source_quote: Serologic studies for CMV, HIV, Rickettsia, and EBV were all negative.

rationale: A 17-year-old male presented with severe chest pain and odynophagia confirmed to have herpes simplex virus (HSV-1) esophagitis on endoscopy and biopsy. Given that herpes simplex esophagitis typically suggests immunocompromise, infectious disease serological testing was performed, and HIV serology was explicitly negative. Because HIV was evaluated and confirmed absent, the case is negative -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 30-year-old woman with neurofibromatosis type 1 and HIV infection presenting with metastatic somatostatinoma/gastrinoma

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection with CD4 count of 290 cells/microL co-occurring with neurofibromatosis type 1 and metastatic neuroendocrine tumor

evidence_items.source_quote: She had tested HIV-positive a few months earlier, with a baseline CD4 count of 290 cells/microL.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV testing history and baseline CD4 count

rationale: A 30-year-old woman with known neurofibromatosis type 1 presented with recurrent gastrointestinal bleeds and was diagnosed with a metastatic somatostatin- and gastrin-secreting neuroendocrine tumour. Her medical history notes she had tested HIV-positive several months prior, with a documented baseline CD4 count of 290 cells/microL. Documented positive HIV test and CD4 enumeration confirm target infection presence as a clinical comorbidity. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 27-year-old patient diagnosed with HIV-positive infection in August 2008 followed longitudinally across multiple ART treatment failure episodes

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection with multi-class antiretroviral drug resistance mutations evolving during ART failure

evidence_items.source_quote: A 27-year-old patient was diagnosed as HIV-positive in August 2008.
The patient had been diagnosed as HIV-positive in August 2008 and initiated ART with 3TC+AZT+NVP.

In March, 2015, the ART regimen was changed, to 3TC+AZT+LPV/r+RAL, again due to unsuppressed viral load (5.4*104 copies/mL). By June, 2017, two years later, the viral load had increased, to 1.8*105 copies/mL (Table 1), and was followed by the patient's death in August, 2017.
evidence_items.test_name: ART regimen change and high unsuppressed HIV viral load
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV RNA viral load under therapy

rationale: A 27-year-old patient diagnosed as HIV-positive in August 2008 was followed through multiple lines of antiretroviral therapy (initial 3TC+AZT+NVP, switched to 3TC+AZT+LPV/r, and then augmented with raltegravir). Longitudinal virological tracking demonstrated recurrent treatment failure with viral loads peaking at 1.8 x 10^5 copies/mL and extensive NGS/Sanger genotyping demonstrating accumulation of multi-class resistance mutations across RT, PR, and IN genes. Long-term confirmed diagnosis with extensive quantitative viral loads and genotypic sequencing confirms HIV infection. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.target_concept: HIV infection on ART with CD4 count

rationale: A 49-year-old male presented with fever, malaise, splenomegaly, and lymphadenopathy confirmed as HHV-8-positive multicentric Castleman disease. Documented HIV infection managed on specific triple ART regimen confirms target disease presence as a clinical comorbidity. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 76-year-old male presenting with exertional dyspnea and recurrent hemorrhagic pleural/pericardial effusions, diagnosed with HHV8-unrelated HIV-negative primary effusion lymphoma

rationale: A 76-year-old male presented with exertional dyspnea, weight loss, and large pericardial and pleural effusions, ultimately diagnosed with HHV8-unrelated primary effusion lymphoma. Screening serologies explicitly evaluated HIV, HCV, HHV-8, Lyme, and EBV, and all were confirmed negative. The case report specifically establishes the patient as HIV-negative. step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 51-year-old female with past medical history significant for AIDS presenting with a chronic painful hypertrophic hand ulceration due to resistant HSV

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient has been followed in the HIV clinic for 3 years since treatment and there has been no recurrence of the lesion.

rationale: A 51-year-old African American woman with a documented history of AIDS presented with a hypertrophic right-hand ulceration refractory to oral antivirals, confirmed as dual HSV-1/HSV-2 on biopsy. evidence_items.source_quote: At the moment of our attention, her CD4 count was 250/mm3 and HIV-RNA was lower than 37 copies/mL.
evidence_items.test_name: CD4 count and quantitative HIV RNA
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV viral load and CD4 count

rationale: A 30-year-old woman with a 10-year history of confirmed HIV seropositivity treated with HAART presented for termination of pregnancy and was found to have a heterotopic pregnancy requiring salpingectomy. Documented HIV seropositivity with quantitative viral RNA and CD4 testing confirms the target disease -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 55-year-old male presenting with septic shock from retroperitoneal necrotizing fasciitis secondary to Fournier gangrene and newly diagnosed advanced HIV/AIDS with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia

rationale: A 55-year-old male presented with severe retroperitoneal necrotizing fasciitis extending from Fournier's gangrene requiring extensive surgical debridement. step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 74-year-old Kenyan woman presenting with lower extremity edema, DVT, weight loss, and biliary duct dilatation, newly diagnosed with advanced HIV/AIDS and AIDS cholangiopathy

evidence_items.source_quote: Written consent was also obtained to complete an HIV test.

evidence_items.test_name: HIV serologic test, CD4 count, and HIV RNA viral load

rationale: A 74-year-old Kenyan woman presented with lower extremity DVT, marked unintended weight loss, and biliary/pancreatic duct dilatation on MRCP/ERCP indicative of sclerosing cholangiopathy. step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 60-year-old male presenting with acute severe Babesia microti infection and a transient false-positive fourth-generation HIV test resolved by negative repeat testing and negative HIV-1 RNA

evidence_items.test_name: Fourth-generation HIV 1/2 Ag/Ab assay with antibody differentiation

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient had repeated HIV testing and HIV-1 RNA, which were negative. HIV-1 and HIV-2 viral loads were not tested. The CD4 count was 455.
evidence_items.test_name: Repeat HIV testing and HIV-1 RNA NAT
evidence_items.target_concept: Confirmatory HIV RNA and repeat serology

step10_contradiction_notes: Initial fourth-generation HIV 1/2 antigen/antibody screen was preliminary positive with an indeterminate HIV-2 antibody, but repeated HIV testing and HIV-1 RNA were negative after treatment of acute babesiosis, confirming a false-positive screening assay caused by acute Babesia microti infection.
rationale: A 60-year-old male presented with severe hemolytic anemia and multiorgan dysfunction due to Babesia microti. Initial fourth-generation HIV screening returned preliminary positive with indeterminate HIV-2 antibody differentiation. However, subsequent repeat HIV testing and qualitative HIV-1 RNA NAT were negative following treatment of babesiosis, and his CD4 count was normal (455 cells/muL). The discordance was definitively resolved as a tick-borne pathogen-induced false-positive HIV screening result. Because HIV infection was ruled out, the label is NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 36-year-old male presenting with recurrent Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia and profound CD4 lymphopenia, diagnosed with late-onset combined immunodeficiency (LOCID/CVID) after repeatedly testing negative for HIV

evidence_items.test_name: Serum antibody assays for HIV-1 and -2

evidence_items.test_name: Repeat HIV-1/2 antibodies and quantitative HIV-1 plasma RNA

rationale: A 36-year-old male presented with severe Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia and profound CD4 lymphopenia. step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 40-year-old male with HIV-1 infection diagnosed 2 months prior presenting with Hodgkin lymphoma, successfully treated with CHOP and antiretroviral therapy

After eight cycles, the patient was asymptomatic, with reduction in neck swelling and weight gain. His CD4 improved from 166 to 247 cells/mm3, with reduction in size of the mediastinal and abdominal lymph nodes on sonography and CT scan.
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV treatment response with CD4 recovery

rationale: A 40-year-old male diagnosed with HIV-1 infection two months earlier presented with constitutional symptoms and lymphadenopathy confirmed on biopsy as Hodgkin's lymphoma. He was treated concurrently with chemotherapy and triple antiretroviral therapy (stavudine, lamivudine, nevirapine), leading to clinical remission and CD4 improvement to 247 cells/mm3. Established HIV infection with low CD4 count and ART treatment confirms target disease -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.test_name: Repeat HIV ELISA and CD4 T-cell count/percentage
evidence_items.target_concept: Confirmatory HIV serology and CD4 immunophenotyping

rationale: A 5.5-year-old boy whose parents were both known to be HIV-infected presented with chronic failure to thrive, recurrent infections, and generalized lymphadenopathy. step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 42-year-old female presenting with cerebral toxoplasmosis and newly diagnosed HIV infection with profound CD4 lymphopenia (10 cells/mm3) and viral load 66,500 copies/mL

evidence_items.source_quote: She was also diagnosed with HIV at this time and her plasma HIV viral load in January 2017 was 66 500 copies/mL and her CD4 T-cell count was 10 cells/mm3. evidence_items.target_concept: HIV RNA, CD4 count, and resistance profile

evidence_items.test_name: Follow-up HIV viral load and CD4 count

evidence_items.source_quote: her repeat HIV viral load was <40 copies/mL with a CD4 T-cell count of 312 cells/mm3 after 3 months on the new regimen.

rationale: A 42-year-old woman presented with acute neurological impairment and ring-enhancing brain lesions proven to be cerebral toxoplasmosis (an AIDS-defining illness). evidence_items.source_quote: The patient reestablished care in October 2016 at which time she was asymptomatic with a HIV viral load of 325 000 copies/mL, and the CD4 T-cell count was 68 cells/mm3.

rationale: A 35-year-old Hispanic woman with known HIV-1 infection since 2004 was previously suppressed on EFV/FTC/TDF. step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 30-year-old male presenting with new-onset focal seizures and brain masses, diagnosed with cryptococcal granuloma in an immunocompetent host with negative HIV testing

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 39-year-old male with neglected HIV/AIDS (CD4 count 26 cells/muL, viral load 162,000) presenting with jejunal perforation from gastrointestinal histoplasmosis

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 38-year-old Zambian male with HIV-1 infection on cART presenting with pernicious anemia and vitiligo

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 31-year-old male with newly diagnosed HIV infection presenting with prolonged fever and diagnosed with ALK-negative anaplastic large cell lymphoma
