In June 2021, he resumed the follow-up visits showing an alarming viro-immunological profile: high levels of HIV-RNA were detectable and the CD4 cell count was less than 200 cells/mm3. ART and the opportunistic infection prophylaxis were promptly started.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV-RNA viral load and CD4 cell count

evidence_items.source_quote: A reactive switch to an integrase inhibitor (INI)-based regimen containing tenofovir (emtricitabine/tenofovir-alafenamide/bictegravir) was started.

rationale: A 64-year-old Caucasian man with long-standing HIV infection diagnosed in 1984 had received multiple antiretroviral regimens over decades. After a period of being lost to follow-up, he returned in June 2021 with detectable high levels of HIV-RNA and profound CD4 cell depletion (<200 cells/mm3). He was restarted on antiretroviral therapy and subsequently switched to an integrase inhibitor-based regimen (bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide), achieving undetectable viral loads. Documented confirmatory HIV-RNA detection and CD4 immunosuppression on ART establish confirmed HIV infection -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 44-year-old Caucasian woman presenting with fever, ataxia, and progressive confusion, diagnosed with acute HIV infection with seroconversion failure and fatal acute HIV encephalopathy

step5_concept_grounding: Acute HIV-1 infection with seroconversion failure (persistently negative antibody screening ELISAs), fulminant viremia (>500,000 copies/mL), elevated p24 antigen (202 pg/mL), profound CD4 lymphopenia (101 cells/muL), Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, and fatal acute HIV encephalopathy

evidence_items.source_quote: Samples sent on hospital day 9 eventually showed wild-type HIV with a viral load >500,000 copies/mL.
The serum level of HIV p24 antigen was 202 pg/mL.
Two days later, the HIV viral load was 241,789 copies/mL.
evidence_items.test_name: Repeat HIV quantitative viral load PCR

evidence_items.source_quote: Tests on hospital day 2 showed a CD4 count of 101/mL (16.9%).
Autopsy showed acute HIV encephalopathy and cerebral vasculopathy.

step10_contradiction_notes: Repeated HIV antibody screening ELISAs were negative due to humoral seroconversion failure, but plasma HIV RNA viral load (>500,000 copies/mL), serum p24 antigen (202 pg/mL), CD4 lymphopenia (101 cells/muL), and autopsy findings definitively confirmed acute HIV infection.
rationale: A 44-year-old Caucasian woman presented with fever, gait ataxia, and progressive confusion. Although multiple serial enzyme immunoassays were negative due to profound humoral seroconversion failure in a rapid progressor, plasma HIV viral load was extremely high (>500,000 copies/mL and 241,789 copies/mL), serum p24 antigen was elevated at 202 pg/mL, CD4 count was markedly depressed at 101 cells/muL, and autopsy definitively demonstrated acute HIV encephalopathy, cerebral vasculopathy, and Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia. Confirmatory viral RNA quantification, p24 antigenemia, and postmortem histopathology establish confirmed acute HIV infection despite antibody seronegativity -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 43-year-old HIV-positive male presenting with reddish nodular lesions in the bulbar conjunctiva diagnosed as Kaposi's sarcoma

step5_concept_grounding: HIV infection confirmed by screening and confirmatory testing with CD4 lymphopenia (154 cells/mm3) presenting with conjunctival Kaposi's sarcoma treated with excisional biopsy and standard antiretroviral therapy

evidence_items.source_quote: Screening and confirmatory tests were positive for HIV with CD4+ lymphocyte cell count of 154 cells/mm3.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV screening and confirmatory tests and CD4 count

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient initiated standard antiretroviral therapy in January 2011 and remains in followup in the Infectious Diseases Department.

rationale: A 43-year-old male presented with a 3-month history of an enlarging reddish conjunctival mass. Both screening and confirmatory laboratory tests were positive for HIV infection, accompanied by CD4+ lymphocyte depletion (154 cells/mm3). Histopathology and immunohistochemistry (CD31, CD34) confirmed Kaposi's sarcoma. The patient was successfully managed with surgical excision, cryotherapy, and standard antiretroviral therapy without recurrence at 2-year follow-up. Positive confirmatory laboratory testing and AIDS-defining Kaposi's sarcoma fulfill confirmatory criteria -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Qualitative multiple case study examining stakeholder engagement across HIV vaccine trials (including RV144 with 16,402 participants) in four countries; no individual clinical patient

step5_concept_grounding: Stakeholder and community engagement in multinational HIV vaccine clinical trials
rationale: This publication reports a qualitative multiple-case study evaluating stakeholder engagement practices across multinational HIV vaccine trial sites (such as the RV144 trial with 16,402 participants in Thailand, South Africa, Canada, and India). Data were derived from thematic coding of focus groups and interviews with trial staff and community stakeholders. Because this describes an aggregate qualitative research study without an individual clinical care unit (F2_SCOPE_COHORT), it fails CCU criteria -> EXCLUDED_NON_SINGLE_PATIENT.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 56-year-old male with a 6-year history of HIV who stopped ARV therapy, presenting with massive weight loss, pseudomembranous oral candidiasis, and persistent COVID-19

step5_concept_grounding: HIV stage IV infection with wasting syndrome, high viral load, and severe pseudomembranous oral candidiasis complicated by chronic COVID-19 infection, managed with restarted antiretroviral therapy (efavirenz/emtricitabine/tenofovir)

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient was diagnosed with HIV for the last six years and stopped taking ARV medication during the mid-COVID-19 pandemic.

Based on the results of the investigations carried out, the patient has anemia, lymphopenia, also HIV positive with high viral load results, and COVID-19 infection for 8 months. In conclusion, based on the history, clinical examination, and supporting examinations, it was found that the patient was diagnosed with HIV stage IV with wasting syndrome, confirmed COVID-19 severe case, and intraoral diagnosis as pseudomembranous oral candidiasis.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV viral load and clinical staging
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV viral load and stage IV AIDS

evidence_items.source_quote: The management for this case from Department of Internal Medicine were given Co-Trimoxazole (Trimetropin/Sulfamethoxazole), Efavirenz/Emtricitabine, Tenofovir, Lovenox, Enoxaparin Sodium, Anticoagulant, Remdesivir, and Vitamin D 5000 IU.

rationale: A 56-year-old male with a 6-year history of HIV who discontinued antiretroviral medication during the COVID-19 pandemic presented with 25 kg weight loss, burning oral pain, severe pseudomembranous candidiasis, and persistent SARS-CoV-2 infection. Laboratory investigation confirmed HIV-positive status with a high plasma viral load, CD4 lymphopenia, and clinical progression to stage IV HIV/AIDS with wasting syndrome. Treatment was initiated with combination antiretroviral therapy (efavirenz/emtricitabine/tenofovir), cotrimoxazole, and antifungal therapy, leading to complete clinical resolution. Confirmatory high viral load quantification and ongoing management confirm active HIV infection -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 40-year-old man presenting with cervical lymph node tuberculosis and posterior pharyngeal Kaposi's sarcoma, diagnosed with HIV-1 infection and profound CD4 lymphopenia

step5_concept_grounding: HIV-1 infection confirmed by ELISA and Western blot with severe CD4 lymphopenia (18 cells/muL) complicated by cervical lymph node tuberculosis and Kaposi's sarcoma, treated with antiretroviral therapy (zidovudine, didanosine)

evidence_items.source_quote: Both HIV enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay and western blot were positive for HIV-1.
The CD4+ T-cell absolute count was only 18 cells/muL.
He began receiving zidovudine in October in 1996. This was replaced by didanosine (ddI) 1 month later because of refractory bone marrow suppression.

rationale: A 40-year-old man presented with fever, weight loss, cervical tuberculous lymphadenitis, and posterior pharyngeal Kaposi's sarcoma. Diagnostic testing revealed positive HIV ELISA and confirmatory positive Western blot for HIV-1, accompanied by critical CD4+ T-cell depletion (18 cells/muL). He was treated with antimycobacterial agents and sequential antiretroviral therapy (zidovudine followed by didanosine). Conclusive Western blot confirmation and severe immunodeficiency satisfy confirmatory diagnostic criteria -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Prospective cohort study of 50 women with CIN 2 evaluating HPV genotypes and lesion regression; immunodeficiency diseases cited as an exclusion criterion

step5_concept_grounding: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 cohort study protocol and exclusion criteria regarding immunodeficiency
rationale: This text outlines the eligibility criteria, sampling methods, and 1-year follow-up protocol of a prospective cohort study of 50 women with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 (CIN 2) evaluating HPV genotypes. The mention of immunodeficiency represents an exclusion criterion within the study methods. Because the text presents aggregate cohort protocol methodology rather than an individual clinical care unit (F2_SCOPE_COHORT), it fails CCU criteria -> EXCLUDED_NON_SINGLE_PATIENT.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 32-year-old woman presenting with dyspnea, chest pain, and a middle mediastinal mass confirmed as Talaromyces marneffei mediastinitis, testing negative for HIV

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnostic evaluation of mediastinal mass in an immunocompetent patient diagnosed with Talaromyces marneffei mediastinitis; HIV antibody serology was negative

evidence_items.source_quote: T-Spot test suggested positive while other blood tests showed negative for blood culture, cryptococcal antigen latex agglutination test, candida galactomannan antigen test, (1-3)-beta-D glucan antigen test, tumor-associated antigens and HIV antibodies.

rationale: A 32-year-old woman presented with fever, cough, chest pain, and a mediastinal mass compressing the trachea, which was definitively identified on EBUS-TBNA culture and mNGS as Talaromyces marneffei mediastinitis. Given that Talaromyces marneffei is an opportunistic pathogen strongly tied to advanced HIV infection, serum testing for HIV antibodies was performed as an essential differential rule-out; the result was explicitly negative. Target disease HIV is ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 46-year-old gentleman from Bangladesh presenting with invasive Klebsiella pneumoniae pyogenic liver abscess syndrome, testing negative on HIV serology

step5_concept_grounding: Immunological screening in a patient presenting with invasive Klebsiella pneumoniae pyogenic liver abscess syndrome; HIV serology was negative

evidence_items.source_quote: while HIV was excluded with a negative serology.

rationale: A 46-year-old man presented with fever, septic shock, and right upper quadrant discomfort, diagnosed with invasive Klebsiella pneumoniae pyogenic liver abscess syndrome complicated by septic pulmonary emboli and necrotizing gluteal myositis. During the infectious disease workup to evaluate underlying immunocompromise, HIV serology was specifically performed and returned negative. Target disease HIV is ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 31-year-old woman with documented HIV infection for 8 years presenting with confusion and a basal ganglia lesion confirmed as cerebral toxoplasmosis

step5_concept_grounding: Advanced HIV infection documented for 8 years with profound CD4 lymphopenia (14 cells/mm3) and high viral load (206,548 copies/mL) presenting with cerebral toxoplasmosis, responding to antimicrobial therapy and HAART initiation

evidence_items.source_quote: This 31-year-old woman, with documented HIV infection for 8 years, presented with a four-day history of intermittent episodes of confusion associated with headache, fever, productive cough, and dyspnoea.

Baseline laboratory tests revealed a very low CD4 cell count (14 cells/mm3 at 4%) and an HIV viral load of 206,548 copies/mL, indicating that the patient was significantly immunosuppressed and at risk for opportunistic infection.
evidence_items.test_name: CD4 cell count and HIV viral load

evidence_items.source_quote: She was commenced on highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) and was counselled by the genitourinary service regarding the importance of compliance to her HIV treatment in the future.
at which point her CD4 count was noted to have risen to 129 cells/mm3 and 10% and her HIV viral load had reduced to 129 copies/mL.
evidence_items.test_name: Follow-up CD4 count and HIV viral load

rationale: A 31-year-old woman with a documented history of untreated HIV infection for 8 years presented with acute confusion and a left basal ganglia mass demonstrated by biopsy to be cerebral toxoplasmosis. Admission laboratory testing demonstrated profound CD4 immunosuppression (14 cells/mm3) and an HIV viral load of 206,548 copies/mL. Following antiparasitic therapy and initiation of highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART), her viral load suppressed to 129 copies/mL and CD4 count rebounded to 129 cells/mm3. Conclusive viral load quantification and successful response to HAART confirm active HIV infection -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 25-year-old man presenting with acute psychotic symptoms, fever, and pancytopenia, diagnosed with primary HIV-1 infection and visceral leishmaniasis-induced secondary HLH

step5_concept_grounding: Acute HIV-1 infection confirmed by positive serology, immunoblot, and massive plasma viral load (5.47-6.85 million copies/mL) with severe CD4 depletion (30-90 cells/mm3), complicated by visceral leishmaniasis-induced secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH), responding successfully to cART and liposomal amphotericin B

evidence_items.source_quote: HIV-1 serology returned positive, confirmed by immunoblot, with a viral load of 5.47 million copies/mL and a CD4+ T-cells count of 90/mm3.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV-1 serology, immunoblot, viral load, and CD4 count
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV-1 RNA, antibodies, and CD4 T-cells

evidence_items.source_quote: HIV blood viral load at admission (2 weeks after first symptoms) was at 6.85 million copies/mL with a blood CD4+ T-cells count of 30/mm3 and a global lymphopenia (including CD8+ and NK cells).
Combined anti-retroviral therapy (cART) was introduced 2 weeks after diagnosis, consisting in tenofovir, emtricitabine and raltegravir, and Pneumocystis pneumonia was prevented by cotrimoxazole.
Viral load decreased to 75 copies/mL and CD4+ T-cells count increased to 213/mm3 two months after cART initiation and viral load was undetectable with CD4+ T-cells count at 345/mm3 after 6 months
evidence_items.test_name: Post-cART viral load and CD4 monitoring
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV viral suppression and immune recovery

rationale: A 25-year-old man presenting with acute psychotic symptoms, fever, oral candidiasis, and pancytopenia tested positive for HIV-1 by serology and confirmatory immunoblot, with astronomical viral loads (5.47 million to 6.85 million copies/mL) and severe CD4 T-cell depletion (30-90 cells/mm3). Bone marrow biopsy revealed co-infection with Leishmania infantum causing secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH). Following treatment with liposomal amphotericin B and combined antiretroviral therapy (tenofovir, emtricitabine, raltegravir), the patient fully recovered, achieving complete viral suppression and CD4 count recovery to 345 cells/mm3. Conclusive serology, immunoblot, and multi-million copy viral load satisfy confirmatory criteria -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 25-year-old man with visceral leishmaniasis and HIV co-infection undergoing retrospective incidence immunoassay to determine infection duration

step5_concept_grounding: Co-infection of visceral leishmaniasis and HIV causing secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis, evaluated retrospectively by incidence immunoassay and confirmatory immunoblot

evidence_items.source_quote: Thus, the diagnosis of secondary HLH caused by visceral leishmaniasis and HIV co-infection was established.

In order to date the HIV infection, an incidence immunoassay designed for HIV surveillance and based on antibody binding to the gp41 and gp120 glycoproteins was performed retrospectively on the two samples with positive immunoblot, which had identical patterns.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV incidence immunoassay and confirmatory immunoblot

rationale: In this continuation segment describing the clinical episode of the 25-year-old man with secondary HLH caused by visceral leishmaniasis and HIV co-infection, an incidence immunoassay targeting gp41 and gp120 glycoproteins was retrospectively performed on two serial serum samples that each demonstrated positive confirmatory immunoblot patterns. Conclusive positive immunoblot findings and confirmed diagnosis of HIV co-infection establish confirmatory diagnostic criteria -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 39-year-old Caucasian male with chronic HIV on HAART since 1995 who received a living related kidney transplant and subsequently developed fatal NRTI-induced lactic acidosis

step5_concept_grounding: Chronic HIV infection on long-term HAART (abacavir, nevirapine, lamivudine) with CD4 reconstitution (500 cells/muL) and suppressed viral load (<40 copies/mL), complicated by fatal NRTI-related lactic acidosis and microvesicular hepatic steatosis following kidney transplantation and tacrolimus interaction

evidence_items.source_quote: A 39-year-old Caucasian male with chronic kidney disease due to a combination of kidney stones and high blood pressure was found to have HIV infection and commenced HAART in 1995 consisting of abacavir, nevirapine, and lamivudine, on which he achieved reconstitution of CD4 count (500 cells/muL) and undetectable HIV RNA viral load (<40 copies/mL).
evidence_items.test_name: HIV diagnosis, HAART history, CD4 count, and HIV RNA viral load
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV RNA suppression and CD4 recovery on HAART

evidence_items.source_quote: Antiretroviral drug levels tested posthumously on stored serum samples lay within the therapeutic range (Table 1).

rationale: A 39-year-old Caucasian male diagnosed with HIV had received combination antiretroviral therapy (abacavir, nevirapine, lamivudine) since 1995, maintaining full CD4 reconstitution (500 cells/muL) and undetectable HIV viral loads (<40 copies/mL). Following kidney transplantation and conversion of immunosuppression to tacrolimus, he developed profound refractory lactic acidosis and multi-organ failure. Postmortem analysis revealed severe microvesicular hepatic steatosis classic for nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) toxicity with therapeutic serum ARV levels. Established HIV infection confirmed by ongoing virologically suppressive HAART meets confirmatory criteria -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 36-year-old male with HIV diagnosed in 2012 on ARV therapy with CD4 count of 31 cells/muL, presenting with giant eyelid molluscum contagiosum

step5_concept_grounding: Stage 2 HIV infection on antiretroviral therapy with severe CD4 lymphopenia (31 cells/muL) presenting with giant molluscum contagiosum of the eyelids successfully treated with topical 20% KOH solution

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient was diagnosed with HIV in 2012 and started ARV therapy in 2017. CD4+ value was 31 cells/muL.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV diagnosis, ARV therapy, and CD4+ count
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV infection on ART with CD4 cell count

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient was diagnosed with giant MC on the eyelids and stage 2 HIV.

rationale: A 36-year-old male diagnosed with HIV in 2012 and established on antiretroviral therapy since 2017 presented with proliferating pruritic facial papules that formed giant confluent eyelid molluscum contagiosum. Laboratory evaluation showed severe immunodeficiency with a CD4+ T-cell count of 31 cells/muL. The extensive molluscum lesions were successfully resolved with topical 20% potassium hydroxide applications. Established HIV diagnosis on ongoing antiretroviral therapy accompanied by severe CD4 cell depletion fulfills confirmatory criteria -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 26-year-old female with HIV diagnosed in 2016 on routine ARVs with CD4 count of 46 cells/muL, presenting with giant eyelid molluscum contagiosum

step5_concept_grounding: Stage 2 HIV infection on routine antiretroviral therapy with severe CD4 lymphopenia (46 cells/muL) presenting with confluent giant eyelid molluscum contagiosum resolving after topical 20% KOH application

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient was diagnosed with HIV in 2016 and consumed ARV routinely. CD4+ value was 46 cells/muL.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV diagnosis, routine ARV therapy, and CD4+ count
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV infection on ARV with CD4 cell count

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient was diagnosed with giant MC on the eyelid and stage 2 HIV.

rationale: A 26-year-old female with HIV diagnosed in 2016 on routine antiretroviral therapy presented with rapidly multiplying confluent papules on her left upper and lower eyelids confirmed on Tzanck smear as giant molluscum contagiosum. Laboratory evaluation confirmed severe immunocompromise with a CD4+ T-cell count of 46 cells/muL. The lesions resolved completely within four weeks of self-administered topical 20% KOH solution. Confirmed HIV infection established on antiretroviral therapy with severe CD4 depletion fulfills criteria -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 35-year-old man diagnosed with HIV stage II and reactive anti-HIV immunoserology, presenting with secondary syphilis oral mucous patches and ocular syphilis

step5_concept_grounding: HIV stage II infection confirmed by reactive anti-HIV immunoserology, presenting with secondary syphilis oral mucous patch, ocular syphilis, and hepatitis B co-infection

evidence_items.source_quote: A 35-year-old man diagnosed with HIV stage II was referred to the Oral Medicine Specialist, Dr. Central General Hospital Hasan Sadikin, Bandung, with secondary syphilis, suspected neurosyphilis, Ocular syphilis, and atypical optic neuritis et causa panuveitis ocular dextra sinistra, hepatitis B, and pruritic papular eruption.
evidence_items.test_name: Clinical diagnosis and HIV stage II classification

evidence_items.source_quote: Immunoserological examination of anti-HIV two weeks ago was reactive, hepatitis b surface antigen (HBsAg) chromatography was reactive, Treponema pallidum hemagglutination assay (TPHA) titer was reactive with titer 1:10,240, and quantitative venereal disease research laboratory test (VDRL) was reactive with titer 1:256.

rationale: A 35-year-old man presented with oral mucous patches, skin papules, panuveitis, and optic neuritis, and was diagnosed with stage II HIV, secondary syphilis, and hepatitis B. Laboratory evaluation confirmed reactive anti-HIV immunoserology alongside high-titer reactive TPHA and VDRL. Reactive anti-HIV laboratory examination and clinical staging confirm active HIV infection -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 53-year-old man presenting with chronic atrophic candidiasis and angular cheilitis, newly diagnosed with HIV infection following a reactive anti-HIV test

step5_concept_grounding: Newly diagnosed HIV infection confirmed by reactive anti-HIV serology presenting with oral candidiasis and angular cheilitis, referred for antiretroviral therapy management

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient was asked to take an anti-HIV test and the result was reactive. He was referred to Internal Medicine Department for further HIV management.

rationale: A 53-year-old man presented with a 1-month history of oral burning and pain refractory to initial treatment, diagnosed with chronic atrophic candidiasis and bilateral angular cheilitis. Given the presentation of extensive oral candidiasis, diagnostic anti-HIV testing was ordered and returned reactive. The patient was referred to the internal medicine department for comprehensive HIV staging and antiretroviral therapy management. Conclusive reactive HIV testing and clinical referral confirm the diagnosis -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 29-year-old man diagnosed with stage IV HIV with wasting syndrome presenting with necrotizing ulcerative gingivitis and linear gingival erythema

step5_concept_grounding: HIV stage IV infection with wasting syndrome presenting with opportunistic oral manifestations including necrotizing ulcerative gingivitis and linear gingival erythema, alongside latent syphilis and chronic hepatitis B

evidence_items.source_quote: He was diagnosed by the Internist with HIV stage IV with wasting syndrome, hypothyroidism, latent syphilis, chronic hepatitis B, moderate dehydration et causa inadequate intake, stage 1 acute kidney injury (AKI), inflammatory anemia, and malnutrition.
evidence_items.test_name: Internal medicine specialist evaluation and HIV stage IV diagnosis
evidence_items.target_concept: Stage IV HIV infection with wasting syndrome

evidence_items.source_quote: The lesions on the gingiva were diagnosed with necrotizing ulcerative gingivitis (NUG). The lesion on the maxillary anterior gingiva was diagnosed as linear gingival erythema.

rationale: A 29-year-old man was evaluated for excruciating gingival pain, mucosal bleeding, and oral pseudomembranes. Oral medicine evaluation confirmed necrotizing ulcerative gingivitis (NUG) and linear gingival erythema (LGE), hallmark opportunistic periodontal lesions characteristic of severe HIV-induced immunosuppression. Definite specialist clinical diagnosis of stage IV HIV/AIDS and classic opportunistic manifestations fulfill criteria -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 29-year-old man diagnosed with HIV stage IV with wasting syndrome and cerebral toxoplasmosis, presenting with oral CMV ulcerations and oral hairy leukoplakia

step5_concept_grounding: HIV stage IV infection with cerebral toxoplasmosis and wasting syndrome, presenting with oral CMV ulcerations and oral hairy leukoplakia, treated with antimicrobial therapy and antiretroviral therapy

evidence_items.source_quote: He was diagnosed with HIV stage IV with wasting syndrome, sol intracranial et causa toxoplasmosis cerebri, anemia et causa gastrointestinal bleeding, hyponatremia et causa Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone secretion (SIADH), and malnutrition.
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV stage IV with toxoplasmosis cerebri and wasting syndrome

evidence_items.source_quote: Folic acid, clindamycin, co-trimoxazole, and fluconazole were prescribed by the internist, and ARV was given three weeks later.
The painless adherent white corrugated plaques that cannot be scrapped on the lateral of the tongue were diagnosed as oral hairy leukoplakia.

rationale: A 29-year-old man presented with painful swallowing and oral ulcerations alongside an established diagnosis of stage IV HIV with wasting syndrome, intracranial space-occupying lesion due to toxoplasmosis cerebri, and SIADH. Diagnostic evaluation confirmed cytomegalovirus (CMV) oral ulcers (positive CMV IgG and viral DNA PCR) and lateral tongue oral hairy leukoplakia. The patient received antiparasitic therapy, antimicrobial prophylaxis, and subsequent initiation of antiretroviral therapy (ARV), resulting in complete healing of the oral lesions. Stage IV HIV/AIDS confirmed by AIDS-defining cerebral toxoplasmosis and initiation of ARV confirms the diagnosis -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 31-year-old HIV-positive male receiving antiretroviral therapy with CD4 count of 114 cells/mm3 and viral load 76,023 copies/ml, diagnosed with AIDS and disseminated sporotrichosis

step5_concept_grounding: Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) in an HIV-positive patient on antiretroviral therapy with severe immunosuppression (CD4 count 114 cells/mm3, viral load 76,023 copies/mL) presenting with disseminated sporotrichosis

evidence_items.source_quote: Case 2 was a 31-year-old HIV-positive male referred for evaluation of multiple cutaneous ulcers. The patient was under anti-retroviral therapy (efavirenz, stavudine and lamivudine), with CD4 count of 114 cells/mm3 and viral load of 76,023 copies/ml.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV status, antiretroviral therapy, CD4 count, and HIV viral load
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV RNA viral load, CD4 count, and combination ART

evidence_items.source_quote: The second patient was then diagnosed with acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) due to CD4 count and viral load associated with deep fungal infection.

rationale: A 31-year-old HIV-positive male under antiretroviral therapy (efavirenz, stavudine, lamivudine) was evaluated for diffuse cutaneous and oral ulcers. Laboratory testing revealed marked immunosuppression with a CD4 count of 114 cells/mm3 and an elevated HIV viral load of 76,023 copies/mL. Biopsy and fungal culture confirmed disseminated Sporothrix schenckii infection, establishing a definitive diagnosis of acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS). He was treated with amphotericin B followed by itraconazole, resulting in complete lesion remission. Confirmatory viral load quantification, CD4 lymphopenia, and AIDS-defining systemic fungal infection establish confirmed diagnosis -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 60-year-old Hispanic female with established HIV infection on HAART for over 10 years presenting with tenofovir-associated hypophosphatemia

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection managed with long-term HAART (tenofovir/emtricitabine and fosamprenavir) complicated by tenofovir-induced renal phosphate wasting

evidence_items.source_quote: HIV on highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) therapy for more than 10 years, compliant with her medications
Her HAART medications included tenofovir/emtricitabine with fosamprenavir.

rationale: A 60-year-old Hispanic female with long-standing HIV infection on HAART for more than 10 years (tenofovir/emtricitabine and fosamprenavir) presented with nausea, vomiting, severe fatigue, and profound hypophosphatemia due to tenofovir-induced renal phosphate wasting. step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A male patient with myasthenia gravis treated with corticotherapy who developed iatrogenic Kaposi sarcoma, tested negative for HIV

step5_concept_grounding: Evaluation and rule-out of HIV-1 and HIV-2 infection in a patient presenting with Kaposi sarcoma secondary to immunosuppressive corticotherapy for myasthenia gravis

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient was found to be HHV-8 IgG positive and HIV 1/2 and HTLV I/II negative.

rationale: A male patient with myasthenia gravis treated with corticosteroids developed cutaneous lesions confirmed histologically as Kaposi sarcoma. The patient tested explicitly negative for HIV-1/2 ('The patient was found to be HHV-8 IgG positive and HIV 1/2 and HTLV I/II negative'), demonstrating an HHV-8-driven iatrogenic KS rather than epidemic AIDS-related KS. Target disease is ruled out by negative laboratory testing -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 46-year-old woman who attended HIV voluntary counseling and testing following sexual cohabitation, confirmed HIV-1 positive by ELISA and Western blot

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) infection confirmed by enzyme immunoassay and Western blot assay

evidence_items.source_quote: HIV-1 infection status was determined by an enzyme immunoassay (Diagnostic Kit for Antibodies to Human Immunodeficiency Virus Type 1 and 2 (ElISA), bioMerieux sa, France) and confirmed by Western blot assay (HIV BLOT 2.2, MP Diagnostics, Singapore).
evidence_items.test_name: Enzyme immunoassay and Western blot assay

evidence_items.source_quote: On May 14, 2013, the woman was confirmed to be infected with HIV-1.

rationale: A 46-year-old woman attended an HIV voluntary counseling and testing clinic after discovering her partner's undisclosed HIV-positive status. Diagnostic blood sampling demonstrated HIV-1 reactivity via screening enzyme immunoassay (bioMerieux ELISA) and definitive confirmation by Western blot (HIV BLOT 2.2). On May 14, 2013, she was confirmed to be infected with HIV-1. Repeat Western blot testing during forensic transmission analysis reaffirmed HIV-1 infection. Documented confirmatory Western blot satisfies E1 gold-standard diagnostic criteria -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 32-year-old female with HIV infection, defaulted Atripla for one year with severe CD4 lymphopenia (86/microL), presenting with chronic multiple lung abscesses

evidence_items.source_quote: A 32 years-old female, HIV positive who defaulted using Atripla for over a period of one year with current CD4 of 86/microL was referred to a tertiary hospital with chest x-ray showing a lesion suspicious of a lung tumour.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV status, antiretroviral history, and CD4 cell count
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV infection and CD4 cell count

rationale: A 32-year-old female with established HIV infection who had defaulted on her antiretroviral therapy (Atripla) for over one year presented with chronic multiple lung abscesses and bronchiectasis. step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 3-year-old uninfected male child who accidentally ingested four and a half bottles of abacavir/lamivudine prescribed for his HIV-positive stepbrother

evidence_items.source_quote: This was 24 hours after ingesting four and a half bottles of abacavir 600 mg/lamivudine 300 mg combination pills prescribed for his stepbrother.

rationale: A 3-year-old male child presented following accidental toxic ingestion of a massive overdose of abacavir/lamivudine antiretroviral tablets prescribed for his stepbrother. Diagnostic testing confirmed that the patient was uninfected ('His HIV test was negative'). Per explicit project curation guidelines, cases involving accidental ingestion of antiretroviral medication by an uninfected person represent non-target toxicological presentations and subject coreference confusion (F3_SUBJECT_COREFERENCE) -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 33-year-old HIV-infected male on tenofovir/emtricitabine and efavirenz with CD4 >500 and undetectable viral load presenting with Chlamydia proctitis and Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 25-year-old man from Ghana presenting with altered mental state and respiratory symptoms, newly diagnosed with HIV/AIDS (CD4 <20, high viral load) and disseminated Cryptococcus neoformans

evidence_items.target_concept: HIV RNA, antibody, and CD4 count

rationale: A 25-year-old man presented with fever, altered mental status, photophobia, and weight loss. step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 54-year-old male potential FMT donor who had a false-positive screening HIV p24 antigen, with HIV ruled out by negative Multispot differentiation assay and undetectable viral load

step5_concept_grounding: False-positive HIV screening assay ruled out by negative Multispot HIV-1/HIV-2 differentiation assay and negative HIV viral load

evidence_items.source_quote: As part of routine screening to evaluate his suitability as a donor, the son's HIV p24 antigen returned positive.
Confirmatory testing using a Multispot HIV-1 and HIV-2 antibody differentiation assay returned as negative, and subsequent HIV viral load was negative.
evidence_items.test_name: Multispot HIV-1/2 antibody differentiation assay and HIV viral load

evidence_items.source_quote: The son was then counseled that he had a false-positive HIV test by an infectious diseases physician.

step10_contradiction_notes: Initial screening HIV p24 antigen was reactive, but definitive confirmatory testing with Multispot HIV-1/HIV-2 differentiation assay and HIV RNA viral load PCR was negative, resolving the initial screening test as a false-positive.
rationale: A 54-year-old male underwent routine screening as a prospective fecal microbiota transplant donor for his father. An initial screening test returned positive for HIV p24 antigen. However, confirmatory testing with a Multispot HIV-1 and HIV-2 antibody differentiation assay was negative, and subsequent quantitative HIV RNA viral load testing was negative. An infectious disease physician concluded that the patient had a false-positive screening result. The contradiction between reactive screening antigen and negative confirmatory molecular/differentiation testing is fully resolved as negative. HIV is ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 43-year-old male presenting with unilateral facial nerve palsy, newly diagnosed with acute HIV-1 infection with viral load of 1,030,000 copies/mL and CD4 of 172

Confirmatory tests proved to be positive as well, indicating an acute HIV-1 infection with viral RNA at the time of diagnosis, which resulted in 1,030,000 (PCR log10 6.013).
evidence_items.test_name: HIV-1 confirmatory testing and quantitative viral RNA PCR

evidence_items.source_quote: Initial CD4 counts were depressed with an absolute CD4 count of 172.

rationale: A 43-year-old male presented with acute unilateral peripheral facial nerve palsy. Diagnostic evaluation revealed reactive HIV-1 Ag/Ab screening, positive confirmatory testing, and a very high HIV RNA viral load of 1,030,000 copies/mL (log10 6.013) with a CD4 count of 172 cells/microL, establishing acute HIV-1 infection. He was initiated on antiretroviral therapy (bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF) and opportunistic infection prophylaxis. Conclusive viral RNA quantitation and confirmatory serology fulfill E1 confirmatory lab criteria -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 54-year-old male with cryptococcal meningitis and idiopathic CD4 lymphocytopenia in whom HIV-1 and HIV-2 were definitively ruled out by ELISA and PCR

evidence_items.source_quote: ELISA for HIV-1 and HIV-2 and PCR for HIV-1 and HIV-2 were negative.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV-1 and HIV-2 ELISA and PCR
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV-1 and HIV-2 antibody and RNA

evidence_items.source_quote: Once the diagnosis of cryptococcal meningitis was made, the first and foremost differential was HIV infection, but that was ruled out.

rationale: A 54-year-old male presented with cryptococcal meningitis and was found to have marked CD4 lymphocytopenia (CD4 count 200/mm3). Both ELISA and PCR for HIV-1 and HIV-2 were repeatedly negative ('ELISA for HIV-1 and HIV-2 and PCR for HIV-1 and HIV-2 were negative'), and the clinical team explicitly ruled out HIV infection, establishing idiopathic CD4 lymphocytopenia (ICL). Complete negative diagnostic evaluation definitively excludes target disease -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 34-year-old male with nephrotic syndrome on corticosteroid therapy who developed disseminated cutaneous and systemic Cryptococcus neoformans, tested negative for anti-HIV antibodies

evidence_items.source_quote: In addition, the anti-HIV antibodies, anti-citrullinated peptide antibodies (ACPA), anti-nuclear antibodies (ANA), and anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA) were all tested negative.

rationale: A 34-year-old male on triamcinolone for nephrotic syndrome presented with ulcerated lower-extremity lesions and septic shock from disseminated Cryptococcus neoformans. step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 61-year-old diabetic female with CMV retinitis post-intravitreal bevacizumab, tested negative for HIV antigen and antibodies with normal CD4 count

rationale: A 61-year-old woman with diabetic retinopathy developed CMV retinitis following intravitreal bevacizumab and panretinal photocoagulation. HIV infection is ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Antiretroviral therapy was continued on the ICU with ritonavir-boosted lopinavir and saquinavir.

rationale: A 46-year-old woman with confirmed HIV infection since 2005 on long-term HAART, with a history of opportunistic infections (PCP, CMV pneumonitis), presented with HIV-associated multicentric Castleman's disease and multiorgan failure. Documented chronic HIV on HAART with laboratory monitoring confirms diagnosis -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 19-year-old male who developed Fournier's gangrene following voluntary medical male circumcision, tested negative for HIV

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 52-year-old male who developed necrotizing soft tissue infection/Fournier's gangrene post-circumcision, tested negative for HIV

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A young homosexual male diagnosed as HIV-positive one year prior who deferred standard therapy, presenting with bilateral CMV retinitis and CD4 count of 267/mm3

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 45-year-old male with positive HIV ELISA and CD4 count of 210/muL presenting with post-kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis

rationale: A 45-year-old male presented with nodular skin plaques and lymphadenopathy, diagnosed with post-kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis (PKDL). Positive HIV serology with CD4 lymphopenia fulfills confirmatory diagnostic criteria -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 52-year-old HIV-positive male with CD4 count of 170/muL presenting with post-kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis, referred to ART center for first-line antiretroviral therapy

evidence_items.test_name: Referral to ART center and initiation of first-line antiretroviral therapy

rationale: A 52-year-old HIV-positive male presented with cutaneous leishmaniasis (PKDL). step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 50-year-old male with silicosis and Mycobacterium sherrisii pulmonary infection, tested negative for HIV

rationale: A 33-year-old woman with confirmed HIV infection and severe immunosuppression (baseline CD4 count 30 cells/ul) who had been receiving antiretroviral therapy for ten months presented with giant condyloma acuminatum (Buschke-Lowenstein tumor) of the vulva requiring radical surgical excision. step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 54-year-old female post-allogeneic stem cell transplantation presenting with uterine and ovarian plasmablastic lymphoma, tested negative for HIV

rationale: A 43-year-old male with a documented past medical history of HIV infection, bipolar disorder, and epilepsy was admitted for evaluation of recurrent syncopal episodes, which telemetry revealed to be caused by high-degree AV block secondary to a carotid space mass abutting the vagus nerve. step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 31-year-old Sub-Saharan African woman with known HIV infection for 3 years on ART and cotrimoxazole prophylaxis with CD4 of 155 cells/microL, presenting with peritoneal and intestinal tuberculosis complicated by jejunal perforations

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 14-year-old boy with perinatally-acquired HIV infection on HAART presenting with SSPE

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 40-year-old male presenting with mucocutaneous leishmaniasis mimicking rectal carcinoma

rationale: A 23-year-old female presented with small bowel obstruction and intussusception caused by high-grade large B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. She was diagnosed with HIV four years earlier and remained on combination antiretroviral therapy (tenofovir, emtricitabine, and efavirenz), with laboratory testing confirming an undetectable HIV viral load and a CD4 count of 294 cells/microL. Established HIV infection on ongoing cART with documented viral load and CD4 monitoring confirms the diagnosis -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 40-year-old male presenting with Salmonella empyema and bronchopleural fistula, found to have CD4 count of 26 (3%), without explicit mention of HIV/AIDS in the case narrative

step5_concept_grounding: Evaluation of severe immunosuppression (CD4 count 26) and disseminated Salmonella infection; human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) is ungrounded in the clinical case narrative
rationale: A 40-year-old African American male presented with profound weight loss, night sweats, diarrhea, and Salmonella empyema with bronchopleural fistula, found to have an absolute CD4 count of 26 (3%). Although the article title and abstract indicate that the patient had underlying HIV infection noncompliant with HAART, the target disease HIV/AIDS is entirely unmentioned and ungrounded within the clinical case narrative itself (F5_DISCOURSE_CONTEXT). Because the target disease is not stated or evaluated in the case text, this case is excluded -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 59-year-old African-American man diagnosed with HIV presenting with unmasking coccidioidal meningitis IRIS shortly after ART initiation

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) infection in AIDS stage complicated by fatal unmasking coccidioidal meningitis immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS)

evidence_items.source_quote: Two months earlier, he had sought care for epididymitis; HIV infection was diagnosed at that time (CD4+ T-cell count of 45 cells/microL [7%] and plasma HIV RNA level of 420,720 copies/mL [reference not detectable]).
evidence_items.test_name: HIV viral load and CD4 T-cell count
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV RNA viral load and CD4 count

evidence_items.source_quote: He was started on an ART regimen, and 1 week before his September 2011 illness, HIV RNA level had decreased to 790 copies/mL and CD4+ count had risen to 163 cells/microL (13%).
evidence_items.test_name: HIV viral load and CD4 count monitoring on ART
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV viral suppression and immune recovery on ART

rationale: A 59-year-old African-American man was diagnosed with HIV infection 2 months prior with profound immunosuppression (CD4+ T-cell count 45 cells/microL [7%] and plasma HIV RNA 420,720 copies/mL). Following ART initiation, his viral load dropped to 790 copies/mL and CD4 rose to 163 cells/microL. He presented with severe meningismus, fever, and headache found on autopsy to be fatal unmasking coccidioidal meningitis IRIS. High viral load, CD4 lymphopenia, and response to ART conclusively confirm target HIV infection. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 63-year-old Japanese woman with mixed connective-tissue disease presenting with severe Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, ruled out for HIV

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnostic rule-out of HIV infection in an immunocompromised host on corticosteroid therapy presenting with severe Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP)

evidence_items.source_quote: The HIV antibody test results were negative, and the CD4 count was normal.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV antibody test and CD4 count

rationale: A 63-year-old woman treated with oral steroids for mixed connective-tissue disease developed severe Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia. Diagnostic workup for underlying retroviral immunodeficiency included an HIV antibody test, which was explicitly negative, accompanied by a normal CD4 cell count. As target disease HIV was specifically tested and ruled out, the label is NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 39-year-old Kenyan woman (PAO) with HIV infection on ART since 2010 presenting with advanced cervical squamous cell carcinoma

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection managed with antiretroviral therapy complicated by stage 2B invasive squamous cell cervical cancer

evidence_items.source_quote: PAO is a 39-year-old Gravida 4 Para 4 diagnosed with HIV on 18 January 2010.

She enrolled in HIV care on 22 January 2010, with an initial CD4 cell count of 27 cells/mm3 and has remained at the same facility throughout. She started on ART at enrolment and has visited the HIV clinic on average every 3 months since enrolment.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV clinical care enrollment and ART

rationale: A 39-year-old woman was diagnosed with HIV in January 2010 with a baseline CD4 count of 27 cells/mm3. She was enrolled in longitudinal HIV care, receiving combination ART with regular 3-monthly follow-up visits, and her CD4 count subsequently recovered to 463 cells/mm3. Ten years into HIV care, she presented with invasive stage 2B squamous cell cervical carcinoma. Documented long-term HIV care, profound baseline CD4 nadir, and ongoing ART satisfy diagnostic criteria. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 37-year-old man presenting with persistent fever and bilateral ground-glass opacities, newly diagnosed with HIV and Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia complicated by pneumothorax

step5_concept_grounding: Newly diagnosed human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection with severe CD4 lymphopenia (27/mul) presenting with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia and secondary pneumothorax

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient tested positive for the HIV antigen and his CD4 count was markedly reduced (27/mul).
evidence_items.test_name: HIV antigen assay and CD4 count
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV antigen and CD4 lymphocyte count

evidence_items.source_quote: After providing informed consent, the patient tested positive for HIV. Based on this result and bronchoscopy findings, he was diagnosed with PJP complicated by HIV infection.
The patient subsequently received antiretroviral drug therapy for HIV and was discharged on day 33 after disease onset.

rationale: A 37-year-old man presented with fever and bilateral pneumonia. Diagnostic evaluation revealed positive HIV antigen testing, profound CD4 cell depletion (27/mul), and biopsy/BAL-proven Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (an AIDS-defining illness). He was managed with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, steroids, bronchial occlusion for pneumothorax, and successfully initiated on antiretroviral therapy. Confirmed positive HIV testing with severe immunodeficiency and initiation of ART establishes target disease presence. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 56-year-old female presenting with profuse epistaxis diagnosed with nasopharyngeal plasmablastic lymphoma, explicitly documented as HIV-negative

step5_concept_grounding: Clinical and laboratory exclusion of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) in an adult patient presenting with sinonasal plasmablastic lymphoma

evidence_items.source_quote: A 56-year-old HIV-negative female patient presented with profuse right epistaxis requiring blood transfusion.

rationale: A 56-year-old woman presented with profuse right epistaxis and right nasal obstruction, with biopsy confirming plasmablastic lymphoma (PBL). Given the strong clinical predisposition of PBL in immunocompromised and HIV-positive populations, the patient underwent diagnostic screening and was explicitly documented as HIV-negative. Because HIV infection was evaluated and confirmed absent, the label is NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 46-year-old Ivorian man with HIV/AIDS (CD4 count 115 x 106/l) presenting with tuberculous dactylitis of the left 5th digit

step5_concept_grounding: Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (HIV/AIDS) with severe CD4 T-cell lymphopenia (115 x 106/l) complicated by tuberculous dactylitis and disseminated Mycobacterium tuberculosis

evidence_items.source_quote: A 46 year-old man with HIV/AIDS (CD4 T-cell 115 x 106/l) presented with two weeks of left 5th digit pain and swelling.
evidence_items.test_name: Clinical HIV/AIDS diagnosis and CD4 T-cell enumeration

evidence_items.source_quote: He was not taking antiretroviral medications at the time of presentation.

rationale: A 46-year-old male native of Ivory Coast presented with severe pain and swelling of his left fifth digit due to culture-proven Mycobacterium tuberculosis dactylitis and pulmonary nodules. The patient had documented HIV/AIDS with profound immunosuppression (CD4+ T-cell count of 115 x 106/l) and was not taking antiretroviral therapy at presentation. Documented AIDS with severe CD4 depletion satisfies criteria for target disease presence. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 40-year-old HIV-positive woman on tenofovir/lamivudine/efavirenz presenting with isoniazid-induced subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection managed with combination antiretroviral therapy (tenofovir/lamivudine/efavirenz) developing drug-induced subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus secondary to isoniazid preventive therapy

evidence_items.source_quote: A 40-year-old HIV-positive female presented with an erythematous macular eruption involving the malar and periorbital area, the forehead and neck of six weeks of duration (A).
She had initiated antiretroviral treatment with co-formulated tenofovir/lamivudine/efavirenz QD plus isoniazid preventive therapy (IPT) 18 weeks before with CD4 counts of 496 cells/mul (25%).
evidence_items.test_name: Antiretroviral therapy and CD4 count enumeration

rationale: A 40-year-old HIV-positive female was initiated on combination antiretroviral therapy (tenofovir/lamivudine/efavirenz) and isoniazid preventive therapy (IPT) with a baseline CD4 count of 496 cells/mul (25%). She developed an erythematous facial macular rash diagnosed as isoniazid-induced subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus, which resolved following isoniazid cessation while continuing ART. Confirmed HIV infection managed with active combination antiretroviral therapy fulfills criteria for target disease presence. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 56-year-old man presenting with acute polyradiculoneuropathy (Guillain-Barre syndrome) following acute HIV-1 seroconversion

step5_concept_grounding: Acute human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) seroconversion (HIV-1 RNA 4,400 copies/mL, positive confirmatory antibody) complicated by severe Guillain-Barre syndrome and fatal cardiac arrest

evidence_items.source_quote: Antibodies for HIV-1 were detected, and confirmation test was positive.
CD4+ lymphocyte count was 710/mm3 (45%), and viral load was 4,400 copies of HIV-RNA/mL.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV RNA viral load and CD4 lymphocyte count
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV-1 RNA viral load and CD4 count

rationale: A 56-year-old man presented with rapid progressive quadriparesis, facial palsy, and dysautonomia diagnosed as Guillain-Barre syndrome shortly after a viral prodrome. Diagnostic testing demonstrated acute HIV-1 seroconversion: confirmatory HIV-1 antibody testing was positive, plasma HIV RNA viral load was 4,400 copies/mL, and CD4 count was 710/mm3, having tested negative 6 months prior. Conclusive confirmatory antibody and quantitative HIV RNA viral load establish target disease presence. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 35-year-old male with HIV infection on HAART since 2001 with documented NRTI/NNRTI resistance mutations presenting with non-healing genital ulcers secondary to indinavir

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection managed with second-line protease inhibitor HAART following NRTI/NNRTI resistance mutations, presenting with indinavir-induced genital ulcerations

evidence_items.source_quote: Thirty-five year old unmarried male, known positive for HIV infection and on highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) since 2001, presented with genital ulcers for a prolonged duration of 16 months.

He was initiated on NNRTI containing ART (AZT + 3TC+NVP) in 2001. His CD4 cell count improved in the years 2002-2006 and subsequently in late 2006 he had a decline in CD4 to 140. He underwent genotyping and found to have NRTI and NNRTI mutations. He was switched to boosted indinavir-containing second line HAART regimen in late 2006.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV genotypic resistance assay and second-line HAART

rationale: A 35-year-old male with confirmed HIV infection on HAART since 2001 experienced virologic failure in 2006 with CD4 decline to 140 cells/microliter. Viral genotyping documented NRTI and NNRTI resistance mutations, necessitating a switch to boosted indinavir second-line HAART. He subsequently developed chronic genital ulcers attributed to indinavir toxicity, which completely resolved upon switching to atazanavir. Documented genotypic resistance testing and multi-year antiretroviral management substantiate confirmed HIV infection. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 12-day-old female newborn evaluated for congenital toxoplasmosis born to an untreated HIV-positive mother; infant received nevirapine prophylaxis without documented HIV infection

step5_concept_grounding: Maternal retroviral infection with cerebral toxoplasmosis; non-target neonate evaluated for congenital toxoplasmosis receiving nevirapine prophylaxis without documented infant HIV infection

evidence_items.source_quote: The newborn was delivered at term to her 39-year-old para IV mother who had been diagnosed with HIV infection a year ago but opted out of treatment.

Nevirapine prophylaxis was initiated at birth and the mother opted for exclusive breastfeeding. After a few visits, the newborn was lost from follow-up despite appointments at the pediatric ophthalmology and infectious diseases' clinics and parents being given prescriptions for pyrimethamine, sulfadiazine, and leucovorin.

rationale: A 12-day-old female newborn was evaluated for congenital toxoplasmosis following maternal neurotoxoplasmosis during pregnancy. While the mother had known HIV infection diagnosed one year prior and was started on ART during the third trimester, the primary clinical subject is the newborn infant, who received birth nevirapine prophylaxis but was never diagnosed with nor confirmed to have HIV infection (and was subsequent lost to follow-up). Under subject coreference disambiguation rules, maternal HIV status without infant HIV disease requires exclusion of the non-target case -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 33-year-old Latinx male presenting with right jaw swelling diagnosed with plasmablastic lymphoma, newly testing positive for HIV antigen/antibody

step5_concept_grounding: Newly diagnosed human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection confirmed by HIV antigen/antibody testing presenting with oral plasmablastic lymphoma successfully treated with V-EPOCH and combination antiretroviral therapy

evidence_items.source_quote: He was subsequently tested for HIV antigen/antibody that resulted as positive.
Since the completion of his chemotherapy and with initiation of antiretroviral therapy, the patient remains in remission of his PBL.

rationale: A 33-year-old previously healthy Latinx male presented with right jaw pain and a soft tissue mass confirmed by biopsy to be plasmablastic lymphoma (PBL). Diagnostic workup revealed a positive HIV antigen/antibody test. Following 5 cycles of V-EPOCH chemotherapy, intrathecal methotrexate, and concurrent initiation of combination antiretroviral therapy, he achieved full clinical remission. Confirmatory 4th generation antigen/antibody testing and ART initiation confirm target disease presence. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 35-year-old Indian male soldier presenting with fever, seizures, and altered sensorium, newly diagnosed with HIV-1 encephalopathy and oral thrush

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) infection in AIDS stage (CD4 count 156/mm3, 14%) confirmed by repeat ELISA, presenting with HIV encephalopathy (HIVE) and oral candidiasis

evidence_items.source_quote: His investigations showed that he was HIV-1 reactive.
A repeat testing of HIV by the ELISA confirmed the presence of antibodies against HIV-1. The CD4 count was 156/mm3, with a CD4 percentage of 14%.
evidence_items.test_name: Confirmatory HIV ELISA and CD4 count enumeration

evidence_items.source_quote: He was started on antiretroviral therapy with triple-drug regimens of tenofovir, lamivudine, and efavirenz along with antieplieptics and fluconazole.

rationale: A 35-year-old male soldier presented with fevers, seizures, altered mental status, and oral thrush. Laboratory evaluation was initially HIV-1 reactive and repeat ELISA testing conclusively confirmed antibodies against HIV-1. The CD4 count was markedly reduced to 156/mm3 (14%), and brain MRI demonstrated symmetrical white matter hyperintensities consistent with HIV encephalopathy (HIVE). He was started on triple-drug ART (tenofovir, lamivudine, efavirenz) resulting in cognitive recovery and CD4 count increase to 325/mm3. Conclusive serological confirmation and treatment response confirm target disease presence. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 2-month-old HIV-exposed Nigerian male infant presenting with intermittent fever diagnosed with Plasmodium falciparum malaria, confirmed negative for HIV by PCR

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnostic exclusion of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) via negative polymerase chain reaction in a 2-month-old perinatally exposed infant presenting with Plasmodium falciparum malaria

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood investigations for HIV by polymerase chain reaction were negative.
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV nucleic acid / proviral DNA PCR

evidence_items.source_quote: The mother of the patient was a 38 -year-old nursing officer who was diagnosed to be HIV infected 16 years previously.

rationale: A 2-month-old HIV-exposed male infant presented to the pediatric antiretroviral clinic for follow-up and evaluation of intermittent fevers, ultimately confirmed as Plasmodium falciparum malaria. While both parents were HIV-positive on HAART, diagnostic testing for vertical transmission using HIV polymerase chain reaction (PCR) in the infant was explicitly negative. Because HIV infection was tested and ruled out in the primary patient (F3_SUBJECT_COREFERENCE), the label is NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 54-year-old HIV-infected male on antiretroviral therapy with CD4 count of 140 cells/microl presenting with severe fatal pulmonary Trichosporon/fungal pneumonia

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection with severe CD4 lymphopenia (140 cells/microl) on antiretroviral therapy complicated by fatal invasive pulmonary fungal infection

evidence_items.source_quote: A 54-year-old male, HIV-infected, undergoing antiretroviral therapy, with a history of pulmonary TB, was admitted to the infectious diseases department for dyspnoea, fever and asthenia.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV diagnosis and ART treatment documentation

evidence_items.source_quote: The CD4+ T-cell and CD8+ T-cell counts were 140 cells microl-1 and 180 cells microl-1 respectively, and the CD4+/CD8+ cell ratio was 0.78.
evidence_items.test_name: T-cell subset enumeration by flow cytometry

rationale: A 54-year-old male with established HIV infection on combination antiretroviral therapy presented with dyspnea, fever, and weight loss. Immunological assessment showed advanced immunodeficiency with a CD4+ T-cell count of 140 cells/microl and CD4/CD8 ratio of 0.78. Bronchoalveolar lavage confirmed invasive pulmonary fungal infection (Trichosporon/fungal pathogen). Documented HIV infection managed with active antiretroviral therapy and profound CD4 depletion fulfills clinical criteria for confirmed target disease. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 26-year-old male of Indian origin presenting with oculomotor palsy and multiple intracranial tuberculomas, tested negative for HIV

step5_concept_grounding: Infectious workup ruling out human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection in a patient presenting with central nervous system tuberculosis and multiple intracranial tuberculomas

evidence_items.source_quote: Serology was negative for human immunodeficiency virus infection.

rationale: A 26-year-old male presented with ptosis, left third nerve palsy, and headache, diagnosed with CNS tuberculosis and multiple intracranial tuberculomas on MRI. As part of the workup for underlying immunocompromising states, serological testing for HIV infection was performed and was explicitly negative. Because HIV was evaluated and confirmed absent, the label is NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Health systems research evaluating the operational implementation and retention rates of the antiretroviral adherence club programme at Facility X; no single human patient described

step5_concept_grounding: Health systems implementation study of antiretroviral adherence clubs for adult ART patients at Facility X in Mitchells Plain, South Africa

evidence_items.source_quote: Facility X is an accredited ART initiation and on-going management site, which provides HIV counselling and testing (HCT) and associated support services.

Based on the routine monitoring data of the adherence club programme, an estimated 3,600 patients were receiving ART care at Facility X by the end of 2016 and of these, 1,368 adult patients were retained in care through the adherence club.

rationale: This text describes a health-systems implementation and evaluation study of an antiretroviral adherence club programme at Facility X in Mitchells Plain, South Africa. It analyzes institutional operational data and retention-in-care metrics across a cohort of approximately 3,600 ART patients. Because it represents health services research and program evaluation rather than an individual clinical case encounter (F2_SCOPE_COHORT), the case is excluded -> EXCLUDED_NON_SINGLE_PATIENT.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 59-year-old Moroccan woman presenting with acute hemichorea-hemiballismus, newly diagnosed with HIV/AIDS and cerebral toxoplasmosis

step5_concept_grounding: Newly diagnosed human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection in AIDS stage (CD4 91/mm3, HIV RNA 718,190/ml) confirmed by ELISA and Western blot, presenting with toxoplasmic capsulothalamic abscess and hemichorea-hemiballismus

evidence_items.source_quote: She was found to be HIV positive by ELISA and Western blot analysis.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV ELISA and Western blot confirmatory assay
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV antibodies confirmed by Western blot

evidence_items.source_quote: CD4 cell level of 91/mm3, and Copy numbers of HIV-RNA were 718190 /ml.
evidence_items.test_name: CD4 T-cell count and HIV RNA viral load
evidence_items.target_concept: CD4 enumeration and quantitative HIV RNA

rationale: A 59-year-old Moroccan woman presented with left hemichorea and ballismus, with brain imaging revealing a right capsulothalamic nodular enhancing lesion. Laboratory testing demonstrated that she was HIV-positive confirmed by ELISA and Western blot, with profound CD4 lymphopenia (91 cells/mm3) and a plasma HIV RNA viral load of 718,190 copies/ml, establishing an AIDS-defining cerebral toxoplasmic abscess. Treatment with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole resulted in complete resolution of her movement disorder. Conclusive confirmatory Western blot and high viral load satisfy criteria for target disease presence. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 19-year-old Eastern European male seasonal worker presenting with severe sepsis from Salmonella Enteritidis meningitis, newly diagnosed with HIV-1 in AIDS stage

step5_concept_grounding: Newly diagnosed human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) in AIDS stage (CD4 count 3 cells/mm3, HIV RT-PCR 560,000 copies/mL) presenting with invasive Salmonella enteritidis meningitis and disseminated Mycobacterium avium complex

evidence_items.source_quote: To evaluate this, a 4th-generation HIV-1/HIV-2 antibody and HIV p24 antigen panel was ordered and returned positive. Antibody differentiation confirmed HIV-1 infection. HIV RT-PCR returned 560,000 copies/mL. A CD4 count was obtained showing 3 cells/mm3 and CD4% of 0.4%, confirming AIDS.
evidence_items.test_name: 4th-generation HIV Ag/Ab combo, differentiation assay, RT-PCR viral load, and CD4 count
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV-1 Ag/Ab, viral RNA RT-PCR, and CD4 nadir

evidence_items.source_quote: He was started on elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir alafenamide (Genvoya).

rationale: A 19-year-old seasonal worker presented with severe sepsis and delirium due to Salmonella enterica meningitis and bacteremia. Diagnostic workup for severe immunodeficiency revealed a positive 4th-generation HIV-1/HIV-2 Ag/Ab test, antibody differentiation confirming HIV-1, plasma HIV RT-PCR of 560,000 copies/mL, and a profound CD4 nadir of 3 cells/mm3 (0.4%), confirming AIDS. He was successfully initiated on Genvoya and antimicrobial therapy for concurrent disseminated MAC. Conclusive molecular and serological confirmation establishes target disease presence. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 68-year-old male presenting with progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) in an immunocompetent setting, repeatedly tested negative for HIV

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnostic exclusion of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) in an elderly patient presenting with JC virus-induced progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML)

evidence_items.source_quote: Serologic tests for Borrelia burgdorferi, Treponema pallidum, Herpes simplex virus, measles, Varizella zoster virus, HIV and hepatitis B and C had also been negative.
Further investigations concerning an immunodeficiency were inconspicuous. An HIV-test was negative.

rationale: A 68-year-old male developed visual field deficits, sensory aphasia, and seizures due to JC virus-induced progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML). Comprehensive diagnostic investigations into secondary immunodeficiencies included initial infectious serology as well as repeat specific HIV testing, both of which were explicitly negative with normal lymphocyte subsets. Because HIV infection was tested and confirmed absent, the label is NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A clinical case series of four women with HIV presenting with fever, cough, and cutaneous lesions in Yaounde, Cameroon

step5_concept_grounding: Aggregate clinical series describing four HIV-infected women evaluated for disseminated histoplasmosis in Cameroon

evidence_items.source_quote: Four women with HIV but unknown CD4+ T-cell count were received at the Infectious Disease unit of the Central Hospital Yaounde and at the emergency unit of the Jamot Hospital Yaounde presenting with asthenia, weight loss, productive cough and fever (39 C) as common symptoms for at least 3 weeks.

rationale: This text excerpt describes a multi-patient clinical case series summarizing four women living with HIV admitted to two hospitals in Yaounde, Cameroon, presenting with constitutional and cutaneous symptoms. Because it pools multiple patients in an aggregate clinical summary rather than detailing a single individual patient's clinical care encounter (F2_SCOPE_COHORT), the case is excluded -> EXCLUDED_NON_SINGLE_PATIENT.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Second excerpt from the multi-patient case series describing diagnostic Histoplasma antigen testing across four HIV-infected women and treatment outcomes

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnostic testing and clinical management outcomes across a cohort of four HIV-positive women with disseminated histoplasmosis

evidence_items.source_quote: We performed the Histoplasma antigen tests using the Histoplasma antigen LFA (OIDx company, Scarborough, US). They were strongly positive (0.75) in all four patients (Figure 2).
evidence_items.test_name: Histoplasma antigen LFA in aggregate group
evidence_items.target_concept: Histoplasma antigen testing in HIV cohort

rationale: This excerpt is the continuation of a multi-patient case series evaluating Histoplasma antigen LFA testing and antifungal therapy across four HIV-positive patients. While it details diagnostic confirmation and itraconazole response in one patient, it aggregates diagnostic results across all four patients and discusses loss-to-follow-up for the remaining three. Because it represents a multi-patient case series without a discrete single-patient narrative boundary (F2_SCOPE_COHORT), the case is excluded -> EXCLUDED_NON_SINGLE_PATIENT.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 47-year-old male with an 18-year history of HIV and Kaposi sarcoma on combination ART presenting with primary effusion lymphoma

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) infection on combination ART (raltegravir, ritonavir, abacavir/lamivudine/zidovudine) complicated by HHV-8-associated primary effusion lymphoma (PEL) and Kaposi's sarcoma

evidence_items.source_quote: His medical history was significant for HIV (diagnosed 18 years ago), KS, and chronic left-leg edema secondary to pelvic infiltration of KS, compressing the common femoral and superficial femoral veins for which he previously received chemotherapy (paclitaxel, doxorubicin, and then gemcitabine) and electron beam radiation.
evidence_items.test_name: Longitudinal HIV and Kaposi sarcoma history

evidence_items.source_quote: He admitted to being compliant with his current antiretroviral regimen, which included raltegravir, ritonavir, and the combination abacavir/lamivudine/zidovudine.
HIV serology showed an absolute CD4 count of 261 cells/microl and a quantitative HIV-1 RNA level of 220 copies/ml.
evidence_items.test_name: Quantitative HIV-1 RNA viral load and CD4 count
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV-1 viral load and CD4 enumeration

rationale: A 47-year-old male with an 18-year history of HIV and pelvic Kaposi's sarcoma presented with abdominal distention due to malignant ascites, confirmed as HHV-8-positive primary effusion lymphoma (PEL). He was adherent to multi-agent ART (raltegravir, ritonavir, abacavir, lamivudine, zidovudine) with an absolute CD4 count of 261 cells/microl and quantifiable plasma HIV-1 RNA of 220 copies/ml. Documented quantitative viral load, CD4 monitoring, and ongoing multi-class antiretroviral therapy establish confirmed HIV infection. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 12-year-old Tanzanian boy diagnosed with HIV and cryptococcal meningitis, presenting with relapsing meningitis/IRIS after starting ART

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection with CD4 nadir 65 cells/microL on combination ART (abacavir, lamivudine, efavirenz) presenting with cryptococcal meningitis relapse / paradoxical IRIS

evidence_items.source_quote: Eleven weeks earlier, he was admitted at the regional government hospital for similar complaints when he was diagnosed with HIV and treated presumptively (cerebral spinal fluid [CSF] evaluation negative; Table 1) for cryptococcal meningitis (CM) initially with 800 mg intravenous (IV) fluconazole (induction therapy) then transitioned to oral 400 mg (consolidation therapy) according to Tanzanian National Guidelines.
evidence_items.test_name: HIV diagnosis and initial cryptococcal meningitis therapy

evidence_items.source_quote: Three weeks after CM treatment, his clinical status improved and he began antiretroviral therapy (ART) with abacavir, lamivudine, and efavirenz.
prior to initiating ART he had a CD4 count of 65 cells/microL. At this admission, his viral load was fully suppressed (HIV RNA <20 copies/mL).
evidence_items.test_name: CD4 count nadir and quantitative HIV RNA viral load
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV RNA suppression and CD4 nadir

rationale: A 12-year-old boy in Tanzania was diagnosed with HIV 11 weeks prior with a baseline CD4 count of 65 cells/microL and initiated on ART (abacavir, lamivudine, efavirenz) following treatment for presumptive cryptococcal meningitis. Seven weeks into ART, he presented with relapsing intracranial symptoms due to cryptococcal meningitis paradoxical IRIS, with laboratory evaluation confirming full virological suppression (HIV RNA <20 copies/mL). Documented HIV diagnosis, CD4 nadir of 65 cells/microL, active triple-drug ART, and virologic suppression satisfy confirmatory criteria. Case is positive -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 34-year-old male IDU diagnosed with HIV in 1993 and HCV coinfection, who initiated cART in 2004 achieving undetectable HIV and spontaneous HCV clearance

step5_concept_grounding: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection with baseline CD4 267 cells/mL and HIV RNA 86,500 copies/mL, coinfected with HCV, successfully treated with combination ART (lopinavir/ritonavir, lamivudine, zidovudine)

evidence_items.source_quote: A 34 year-old man, an injection drug user (IDU), was diagnosed with HIV infection in 1993.
At this point, the patient was asymptomatic, with a CD4+ count of 267 cells/mL, an HIV RNA viral load of 86,500 copies/mL and an HCV RNA viral load of 2,280,000 IU/mL.

evidence_items.test_name: HIV viral load and CD4 count
evidence_items.target_concept: HIV viral load and CD4 count

evidence_items.source_quote: He reported that he was doing well after discharge on his current ART, which consisted of Dolutegravir-Rilpivirine (Juluca) and Entecavir.

rationale: A 36-year-old male with established HIV/AIDS and chronic hepatitis B presented with altered mental status and respiratory failure, subsequently developing life-threatening type B lactic acidosis following reintroduction of Biktarvy. Immunovirological testing confirmed HIV-1 infection with a viral load of 963 copies/mL and CD4 count of 134 cells/muL. Following CRRT and mitochondrial cofactor therapy, Biktarvy was substituted with dolutegravir-rilpivirine (Juluca). Documented HIV viral load and immunosuppression on ART meet confirmatory criteria -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 73-year-old female patient presenting with thoracolumbar pain and spinal tuberculosis (T7-T8 MTBC infection)

step5_concept_grounding: Routine infectious screening for HIV ruled out by negative serum HIV antibody testing

evidence_items.source_quote: Pre-admission evaluations (December 30, 2023) showed: negative serum HIV antibody

rationale: A 73-year-old female presented with recurrent thoracolumbar pain and fever, subsequently diagnosed with spinal tuberculosis (Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex) with T7-T8 vertebral destruction. During initial pre-admission evaluation, comprehensive serological testing including serum HIV antibody was performed and confirmed negative ('negative serum HIV antibody'). HIV infection was investigated and excluded -> NEGATIVE.
